sources.note: Step 100 (milestone): tests whether all Steps 1-99 mechanisms form one coherent closed system. Walks the full Requirement->...->Knowledge->Requirement loop (18 sub-transitions) plus epistemic-integrity and 11 further closure dimensions, all PASS. States the Architecture Closure Theorem (forall T: Valid(T) => Authorized+Observable+Traceable+Verifiable+InvariantPreserving) and a compact transition-system formulation. Gives KnowledgeOS its identity as an executable organizational knowledge/decision/governance/engineering/assurance system, presents the canonical 8-layer architecture diagram, and explicitly separates conceptually-closed from empirically-proven via a 17-row status table (16 PASS, 1 not-yet-established: production implementation proof). Previews Step 101, Architecture-to-Reality Conformance.

rows.anchor: Up to Step 99, we have established individual dimensions... a collection of correct mechanisms does not automatically constitute a correct architecture. Do all these mechanisms form one coherent closed system?
rows.statement: Frames Step 100's central question: whether the individually-validated Steps 1-99 dimensions (Knowledge, Evidence, Inference, Decision, Authority, Execution, Security, Privacy, Evolution, Organization, Resources, Observability) form one coherent closed system, since correct mechanisms alone don't constitute a correct architecture.

rows.anchor: 100.1 — The closure proposition ... Reality→Observation→Evidence→Knowledge→Reasoning→Decision→Authority→Action→Outcome→Observation while simultaneously maintaining Security, Privacy, Provenance, Versioning, Assurance, Evolution. If the loop closes without violating the invariants established in Step
rows.statement: States the closure proposition: the core loop must close without violating any invariant established in Steps 1-99 while maintaining Security, Privacy, Provenance, Versioning, Assurance, Evolution.

rows.anchor: 100.2 — Closure does not mean perfection ... We are not trying to prove KnowledgeOS=Perfect. We are trying to establish the architecture is internally coherent, explicitly bounded, traceable, verifiable, and capable of controlled evolution.
rows.statement: Distinguishes closure from perfection/universal correctness; the realistic claim is internal coherence, explicit boundedness, traceability, verifiability, and capacity for controlled evolution.

rows.anchor: 100.3 — First closure test: Requirement → Knowledge ... Represent Requirement(R). KnowledgeOS transforms this into an explicit semantic constraint Invariant(I_R). Expected: R→I_R. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: a requirement (e.g. 'production deployment requires architecture approval') transforms into an explicit Invariant(I_R); result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.4 — Requirement → Invariant → Architecture ... I_R→ArchitectureConstraint. For example Deployment⇒ApprovedChange. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: an invariant becomes an architectural rule (e.g. Deployment⇒ApprovedChange); result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.5 — Architecture → Implementation ... ArchitectureConstraint→DeploymentGate. Expected: the rule is not merely documented. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: an architectural constraint becomes enforceable implementation behavior (DeploymentGate), not merely documentation; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.6 — Implementation → Verification ... Implementation→Test→VerificationResult. For example UnauthorizedDeployment→Denied. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: implementation generates verification evidence (e.g. UnauthorizedDeployment→Denied); result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.7 — Verification → Runtime ... Deployment→RuntimeInstance. The running instance must remain identifiable. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: the verified implementation is deployed to an identifiable RuntimeInstance; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.8 — Runtime → Observation ... Runtime generates Observation, e.g. DeploymentEvent, linked to ArtifactVersion. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: runtime generates Observation (e.g. DeploymentEvent) linked to ArtifactVersion; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.9 — Observation → Evidence ... Observation→Evidence only with appropriate provenance: source, time, identity, version, context, confidence/quality. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: an observation becomes Evidence only with retained provenance (source/time/identity/version/context/confidence); result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.10 — Evidence → Knowledge ... Evidence→KnowledgeUpdate. For example ObservedDeployment→CurrentArchitectureState. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: evidence updates organizational knowledge (ObservedDeployment→CurrentArchitectureState); result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.11 — Knowledge → Decision ... Knowledge→Inference→Decision. The system preserves Evidence≠Inference≠Decision. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: knowledge supports reasoning (Knowledge→Inference→Decision) while preserving Evidence≠Inference≠Decision; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.12 — Decision → Authority ... Decision→Authority. The system can answer who was authorized to make this decision. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: a decision must be associated with an authorized actor/governance mechanism, answerable to 'who was authorized'; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.13 — Authority → Action ... AuthorizedDecision→PermittedAction. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: an authorized decision becomes a permitted action (AuthorizedDecision→PermittedAction); result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.14 — Action → Outcome ... Action→Outcome. Outcome becomes new observation. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: execution produces Action→Outcome, and the outcome becomes a new observation; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.15 — Outcome → Learning ... ExpectedOutcome≠ObservedOutcome creates new knowledge. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: a mismatch between expected and observed outcome creates new knowledge; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.16 — Learning → Evolution ... Knowledge may result in ModelUpdate, PolicyProposal, ArchitectureChange, ImplementationChange, but only through authorized change mechanisms. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: learning may produce ModelUpdate/PolicyProposal/ArchitectureChange/ImplementationChange, only through authorized change mechanisms; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.17 — Evolution → Verification ... every material change returns to ImpactAnalysis→Verification. Evolution→Verification→Runtime. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: every material change re-enters ImpactAnalysis→Verification→Runtime, closing the evolution loop; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.18 — The loop closes ... R→I→A→C→V→D→O→E→K→R'. K→R' because new knowledge can generate new requirements. That is closure.
rows.statement: States the full closed loop R→I→A→C→V→D→O→E→K→R' (requirement, invariant, architecture, code/config, verification, deployment, observation, evidence, knowledge, new requirement), where K→R' since new knowledge can generate new requirements — this constitutes closure.

rows.anchor: 100.19 — But there is a second closure requirement ... The system must also preserve its epistemic integrity throughout the loop. TruthStatus_{t+1} must not be stronger than what the new evidence justifies. Unknown ⇏ Verified without evidence. Result: PASS
rows.statement: States a second, epistemic-integrity closure requirement: TruthStatus_{t+1} must not be stronger than the new evidence justifies (Unknown ⇏ Verified without evidence); result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.20 — Authority closure ... Action must trace backward to Authorization→Role→Authority. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: authority closure requires every action to trace backward through Authorization→Role→Authority; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.21 — Privacy closure ... Information flow must remain bounded throughout Evidence→Knowledge→Inference→Decision→Output. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: privacy closure requires bounded information flow through the entire Evidence→Knowledge→Inference→Decision→Output chain; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.22 — Security closure ... The system must preserve security invariants across Storage→Processing→Retrieval→Execution. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: security closure requires preserved security invariants across Storage→Processing→Retrieval→Execution; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.23 — Temporal closure ... Every material state must be interpretable relative to time. State(t). Historical states must not be silently rewritten. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: temporal closure requires State(t) interpretability with historical states never silently rewritten; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.24 — Version closure ... A material result must be interpretable using its relevant versions V=(Software,Schema,Model,Policy,Ontology,Workflow). Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: version closure requires interpretability against the full multi-dimensional version tuple V=(Software,Schema,Model,Policy,Ontology,Workflow); result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.25 — Provenance closure ... Every material conclusion must have a backward path Conclusion→Reasoning→Evidence→Source. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: provenance closure requires every conclusion to have a backward path Conclusion→Reasoning→Evidence→Source; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.26 — Responsibility closure ... Every material action must have Actor, Role, Authority, Accountability. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: responsibility closure requires every material action carry Actor, Role, Authority, and Accountability; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.27 — Runtime closure ... The design must be testable against actual runtime behavior. Design↔Runtime. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: runtime closure requires bidirectional testability between Design and Runtime; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.28 — Failure closure ... Failure cannot simply terminate the semantic model. If Action→Failure, the system must produce FailureEvidence and RecoveryState. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: failure closure requires that any Action→Failure produces FailureEvidence and RecoveryState, not termination of the semantic model; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.29 — Concurrency closure ... Concurrent operations must remain Consistent according to their declared consistency model. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: concurrency closure requires concurrent operations remain Consistent per their declared consistency model; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.30 — Resource closure ... If resources become insufficient (ResourceExhaustion), the epistemic state must degrade honestly. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: resource closure requires honest epistemic degradation under ResourceExhaustion; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.31 — Evolution closure ... After change System_n→System_{n+1}, the system must re-enter Verification. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: evolution closure requires every System_n→System_{n+1} transition to re-enter Verification; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 100.32 — The complete KnowledgeOS state machine ... S_t --Evidence,Decision,Action,Change--> S_{t+1}. A valid transition must satisfy S_t⊨Invariants and Transition∈AuthorizedTransitions, and the resulting state must satisfy S_{t+1}⊨Invariants'. This is the central formal structure.
rows.statement: Compresses the whole architecture into a state-transition model S_t --{Evidence,Decision,Action,Change}--> S_{t+1}, requiring S_t⊨Invariants, Transition∈AuthorizedTransitions, and S_{t+1}⊨Invariants' — called the central formal structure.

rows.anchor: 100.33 — Architecture closure theorem ... A KnowledgeOS architecture is closed when every material organizational or software state transition can be represented as an authorized, versioned, observable transition whose resulting knowledge and system state remain subject to the applicable invariants.
rows.statement: States the Architecture Closure Theorem: ∀T: Valid(T) ⇒ Authorized(T) ∧ Observable(T) ∧ Traceable(T) ∧ Verifiable(T) ∧ InvariantPreserving(T), subject to explicitly declared assumptions — the strongest architectural proposition of the sequence so far.

rows.statement: Experiment: a full model-update cycle (M_1→M_2, impact analysis, verification, deployment, runtime confirmation) demonstrates the learning/evolution loop closes; result PASS.

rows.statement: Experiment: persistent runtime drift flows RuntimeObservation→Evidence→Knowledge→GovernanceIssue, letting the organization act on the divergence; result PASS.

rows.statement: States the key architectural closure as bidirectional: top-down Governance→Architecture→Implementation→Runtime, bottom-up Runtime→Observation→Evidence→Knowledge→Governance, together forming Governance↔KnowledgeOS↔Engineering.

rows.statement: Distinguishes KnowledgeOS (Observe→Understand→Govern→Decide→Act→Observe) from an ordinary repository (Store→Retrieve).

rows.statement: Distinguishes KnowledgeOS (Context→Evidence→Reasoning→Assurance→Decision→AuthorizedAction) from an AI wrapper (Prompt→LLM→Response), with AI as one participant, not the architecture itself.

rows.anchor: 100.45 — KnowledgeOS is not merely an architecture repository ... Traditional architecture management ends at Document→Review. KnowledgeOS continues Document→Rule→Implementation→Verification→Runtime→Evidence.
rows.statement: Distinguishes KnowledgeOS's continued chain (Document→Rule→Implementation→Verification→Runtime→Evidence) from traditional architecture management's stopping point (Document→Review).

rows.anchor: 100.46 — KnowledgeOS is not merely governance workflow ... A workflow system knows Who→DoesWhat→When. KnowledgeOS additionally knows Why, BasedOnWhat, WithWhatConfidence, UnderWhichPolicy, UsingWhichVersion, WithWhichEvidence.
rows.statement: Distinguishes KnowledgeOS from an ordinary governance workflow system: beyond Who/DoesWhat/When, it additionally tracks Why, BasedOnWhat, WithWhatConfidence, UnderWhichPolicy, UsingWhichVersion, WithWhichEvidence.

rows.anchor: 100.47 — The architectural identity ... KnowledgeOS is an executable organizational knowledge, decision, governance, engineering and assurance system. Its purpose is maintaining the relationship between knowledge, authority, decisions, implementation, runtime reality and evidence.
rows.statement: Gives KnowledgeOS its precise identity: 'an executable organizational knowledge, decision, governance, engineering and assurance system' whose purpose is maintaining the relationship between knowledge, authority, decisions, implementation, runtime reality, and evidence — not merely storing knowledge.

rows.anchor: 100.48 — The core architecture ... 8-layer diagram: Organization (Roles/Authority/Responsibility) -> Knowledge (Evidence/Claims/Context/Provenance) -> Reasoning (Rules/Models/AI/Uncertainty) -> Decision (Rationale/Scope/Dissent/Confidence) -> Governance (Authority/Policy/Approval/Exception) -> Execu
rows.statement: Presents the canonical 8-layer core architecture diagram: Organization→Knowledge→Reasoning→Decision→Governance→Execution→Runtime→Evidence→(cyclic back to)Knowledge, wrapped by six cross-cutting concerns Security+Privacy+Versioning+Provenance+Assurance+ResourceGovernance.

rows.anchor: 100.49 — The most important boundary ... We have demonstrated Architectural coherence. We have not yet demonstrated Implementation completeness. And we certainly have not demonstrated Production correctness. Conceptually closed ≠ Empirically proven.
rows.statement: States the crucial boundary Conceptually closed ≠ Empirically proven: architectural coherence has been shown, but not implementation completeness or production correctness.

Status table: Semantic coherence PASS, Evidence/provenance model PASS, Decision model PASS, Authority model PASS, Security model PASS, Privacy model PASS, Failure model PASS, Concurrency model PASS, Evolution model PASS, Human/AI governa

rows.statement: Records the Step 101 verdict: crossing from Architectural Theory to Architecture Conformance Engineering, with theory remaining COHERENT and implementation status NOT YET PROVEN — the correct engineering conclusion, not a weakness.

sources.note: Research object measuring effective (dependence-adjusted) hypothesis-space multiplicity, shown empirically to diverge sharply from raw candidate count |H|; no canonical closed-form definition established, with a proposed connection to the equivalence-relation/semantic-equivalence (=_sem) problem.

rows.anchor: |H|=1000 while changing dependence structure. It obtains approximately: N_eff≈940.6, 201.9, 51.1, 9.0 for increasingly dependent spaces. ... |H|=1000, 50 groups versus |H|=50, 50 independent candidates. They produce essentially identical threshold behavior and N_eff. ... |H| is not an adequate measure of hypothesis-space complexity.
rows.statement: Endorses the central KR-NEFF result: holding raw candidate count fixed at |H|=1000 while varying dependence structure yields N_eff of approximately 940.6, 201.9, 51.1, and 9.0; critically, |H|=1000-with-50-groups and |H|=50-independent-candidates produce essentially identical threshold behavior and N_eff, confirming raw |H| is not an adequate complexity measure.

rows.anchor: The experiment demonstrates that an effective multiplicity quantity can be empirically constructed/measured under the chosen null and calibration procedure. It does not yet demonstrate that there exists one uniquely correct universal object: N_eff. ... [EXP] An effective multiplicity measure is empirically meaningful under the tested calibration regime. rather than: 'N_eff is real.'
rows.statement: Corrects the overclaiming phrase 'N_eff is real' to the scoped claim that an effective multiplicity measure is empirically meaningful under the tested calibration regime, since N_eff could vary by null model, test statistic, dependence structure, target error criterion, hypothesis equivalence, evidence channel, or decision loss.

rows.anchor: N_eff ≈ n(1-ρ)^2 on a narrow grid. Then it widened the domain and obtained ratios: 0.34→3.10. It therefore retracted the apparent law. ... A locally good empirical approximation was demonstrated not to be a general law. ... Good fit on a narrow design space ⇏ structural law.
rows.statement: Praises the retraction of an initially promising closed-form fit N_eff~n(1-rho)^2: widening the test domain produced ratio errors from 0.34 to 3.10, leading to explicit retraction; frames this as a genuine [NEG] methodological finding (a locally good empirical approximation is not a general law) rather than a research failure.

rows.anchor: What equivalence relation on hypotheses makes two candidate spaces epistemically equivalent? ... H_i ~_Λ H_j iff they are indistinguishable with respect to the observables relevant to Λ. Then: H/~_Λ gives equivalence classes. A first approximation to effective complexity could then be related to: |H/~_Λ|. But do not adopt this as N_eff. It is a research direction.
rows.statement: Proposes reframing effective complexity via an equivalence relation H_i ~_Lambda H_j (indistinguishable under observables relevant to regime Lambda), with |H/~_Lambda| as a first candidate approximation to effective complexity, explicitly not yet adopted as N_eff -- noting this would connect to the unresolved semantic-equivalence (=_sem) problem, possibly a more fundamental object than N_eff itself.

rows.anchor: groups 1000: admit .487, validate .206, unique determination .468; groups 10: admit .899, validate .789, unique determination .855. ... Hypothesis-space dependence structure can affect downstream epistemic determination even when candidate count is fixed.
rows.statement: Highlights what may be KR-NEFF's most significant finding: varying dependence structure while holding |H|=1000 fixed changes downstream rates substantially (admit rate .487 vs .899, validation rate .206 vs .789, unique-determination rate .468 vs .855 for 1000 vs 10 independent groups) -- the effect propagates through Complexity->Admissibility->Validation->Determination, not merely a screening-stage artifact.

rows.anchor: What the experiment directly establishes is: dependence structure changes determination rate. Calling the independent-group count 'complexity' is an interpretation. So the clean status should be: [EXP] Dependence structure affects determination under the tested model. Then: [PROP] This dependence structure is a component of effective hypothesis complexity.
rows.statement: Separates the directly-established [EXP] finding (dependence structure affects determination rate under the tested model) from the interpretive [PROP] claim (dependence structure is a component of effective hypothesis complexity), cautioning against conflating the measured effect with the complexity-theoretic label.

rows.anchor: |𝓗| ≢ effective epistemic complexity(𝓗) with supporting evidence ... N_eff≈9, 51, 202, 941 depending on dependence structure. And a second candidate invariant: Same candidate count does not imply same evidential burden. And a third: Validation independence is a property of evidence-channel relations, not of the validation label.
rows.statement: Proposes three candidate invariants for the research registry: |H| is not equivalent to effective epistemic complexity (evidenced by N_eff ranging ~9 to ~941 at fixed |H|=1000); same candidate count does not imply same evidential burden; and validation independence is a property of evidence-channel relations, not merely a validation component's label.

rows.anchor: Do not add candidate_count to Theory v1.2. Do not add N_eff=n(1-ρ)^2. Do not promote N_eff to a canonical KnowledgeOS primitive. Do not modify v1.2 yet.
rows.statement: Endorses the KR-NEFF experiment's own governance constraints: do not add a candidate_count parameter to v1.2, do not add the retracted closed-form N_eff=n(1-rho)^2, do not promote N_eff to a canonical primitive, and do not modify v1.2.

rows.anchor: I would not say that N_eff necessarily 'feeds an admissibility function that presupposes ≽'. ... Statistical admissibility: N_eff → Multiplicity Control → Threshold which does not necessarily require a general epistemic ordering. Epistemic admissibility: N_eff → Assessment → ≽ → Admissibility. ... N_eff and ≽ should remain related but independent research problems until demonstrated otherwise.
rows.statement: Corrects an over-hasty linkage claim: N_eff does not necessarily require the unresolved epistemic-status ordering (>=) -- a purely statistical admissibility path (N_eff->MultiplicityControl->Threshold) may not need a general ordering, distinct from an epistemic admissibility path (N_eff->Assessment->>=->Admissibility) that does; the two should remain related-but-independent research problems pending further evidence.

rows.anchor: Candidate Space → Multiplicity → Dependence Structure → Effective Complexity → Evidence Burden → Assessment → Validation → Determination. But the mathematical definition of Effective Complexity remains open. ... I suspect these two research lines will eventually meet at: semantic equivalence / indistinguishability.
rows.statement: Updates the research map to Candidate Space->Multiplicity->Dependence Structure->Effective Complexity->Evidence Burden->Assessment->Validation->Determination, with Effective Complexity's mathematical definition left open, and hypothesizes this line and the Structure->Projection->Information Loss->Invariant Preservation line will eventually converge at semantic equivalence/indistinguishability -- 'how many genuinely distinguishable alternatives does the epistemic system actually have?' as a deeper question than raw hypothesis count.

rows.anchor: Scope corrected. This section originally said 'N_eff is real'. Too strong: the experiment shows an effective multiplicity quantity can be empirically constructed under the tested null, test statistic and calibration procedure. It does not show there is one uniquely correct universal object N_eff.
rows.statement: Self-correction: retracts the original overclaim 'N_eff is real' to the scoped claim that an effective multiplicity quantity can be empirically constructed under the specific tested null/statistic/calibration procedure, not that a single universal N_eff object exists.

rows.anchor: independent 1000/1000 groups τ=3.876 N_eff=940.6 ... grouped 1000/50 groups τ=3.097 N_eff=51.1 ... independent |H|=50/50 groups τ=3.097 N_eff=51.1 ... correlated ρ=0.9 N_eff=9.0. A 1000-candidate space with 50 groups is empirically indistinguishable from a 50-candidate independent space -- identical τ (3.097) and identical N_eff (51.1). ... |H| overstates the multiplicity burden by up to 111×.
rows.statement: [EXP]: measures N_eff (inverting a Bonferroni threshold calibrated on the empirical 95th percentile of max score over 4000 null-world trials) across six candidate-space configurations of equal or varying |H|; a 1000-candidate space with 50 independent groups is empirically indistinguishable (identical tau=3.097, identical N_eff=51.1) from a genuinely independent 50-candidate space; at rho=0.9 correlation, 1000 candidates behave like 9 (N_eff=9.0); raw |H| overstates the true multiplicity burden by up to 111x.

experiment.hypothesis: Raw candidate count |H| is an inadequate measure of hypothesis-space multiplicity burden; an effective count N_eff calibrated to dependence structure is the relevant quantity
experiment.setup: NULL world; tau = empirical 95th percentile of max score over 4000 trials; N_eff read off by inverting Bonferroni
experiment.assumptions: a Bonferroni-style multiplicity correction model applies
experiment.inputs: six spaces: independent |H|=1000; grouped 1000/200groups; grouped 1000/50groups; independent |H|=50; correlated rho=0.5 (|H|=1000); correlated rho=0.9 (|H|=1000)
experiment.method: compute tau and invert to get N_eff for each space
experiment.result: N_eff = 940.6, 201.9, 51.1, 51.1, 200.6, 9.0 respectively (matching structurally-equivalent spaces exactly)
experiment.interpretation: |H| is the wrong quantity; effective complexity (N_eff) governs multiplicity burden
experiment.limitations: specific to the tested null/statistic/calibration procedure
experiment.conclusion: [EXP]

rows.anchor: Step 1 -- I asserted, before checking. ... Step 2 -- the assertion was wrong on the evidence I had. n(1-ρ)² fitted well [mean log ratio error 0.082] ... Step 3 -- widening the grid refuted n(1-ρ)². Across ρ∈[0.05,0.95] and n∈[200,5000]: ratio spans 0.34 → 3.10. ... The good fit on the original grid was coincidence of the grid.
rows.statement: Records a three-step self-correction sequence in full: an unchecked assertion that no closed form fits (made before reading the actual error column), followed by discovering n(1-rho)^2 actually fit well on the original six-point grid (mean log-ratio error 0.082, versus 0.599 for n(1-rho), 0.791 for Cheverud M_eff, 1.873 for raw |H|), followed by widening the grid across rho in [0.05,0.95] and n in [200,5000] and finding the ratio spans 0.34 to 3.10 -- a factor of 9 -- refuting n(1-rho)^2 as a general law; the original good fit was a coincidence of the narrow grid.

experiment.hypothesis: N_eff has a closed-form expression n(1-rho)^2 over (n, rho, grouping)
experiment.setup: test the fitted formula n(1-rho)^2 against measured N_eff over a widened grid of rho in [0.05,0.95] and n in [200,5000]
experiment.assumptions: the six-point-grid fit generalizes
experiment.method: compare measured N_eff to n(1-rho)^2 predicted value, compute ratio
experiment.result: ratio ranges from 0.34 (n=5000) to 3.10 (n=200) at rho=0.9, and the n-dependence is plainly wrong
experiment.interpretation: n(1-rho)^2 is refuted as a general law but remains a usable local approximation near n~1000
experiment.limitations: confined to the tested (rho,n,g) grid
experiment.conclusion: [NEG] N_eff is measurable but not reducible to any tested closed form over (n,rho,g); formalizing N_eff is a genuine open mathematical problem

rows.anchor: groups 1000: admit .487 validate .206 unique .468 ... groups 10: admit .899 validate .789 unique .855. Effective complexity affects all three. Admissibility (0.49→0.90), validation (0.21→0.79) and unique determination (0.47→0.86) all move monotonically with the number of independent groups, at constant |H|. ... complexity is not confined to admissibility. It reaches determination.
rows.statement: [EXP]: holding |H|=1000 fixed and varying only the number of independent groups (1000/200/50/10) at signal=0.6, m=40, admissibility rate rises 0.487->0.899, validation rate 0.206->0.789, and unique-determination rate 0.468->0.855, all monotonically with fewer/larger groups -- confirming dependence structure affects determination, not merely admissibility, split into [EXP] (dependence changes determination rate) and the separate, weaker [PROP] (dependence structure is a component of effective complexity).

experiment.hypothesis: Hypothesis-space dependence structure affects downstream epistemic determination, not only initial admissibility screening
experiment.setup: fix |H|=1000, vary independent-group count (1000,200,50,10), signal=0.6, m=40
experiment.assumptions: admissibility threshold computed on |H| vs on N_eff
experiment.inputs: the four grouping configurations
experiment.method: measure admit rate, validate rate, and unique-determination rate at each grouping level
experiment.result: all three rates increase monotonically as group count decreases (fewer, larger groups) at fixed |H|
experiment.interpretation: effective complexity propagates through the entire pipeline (admissibility, validation, determination), not just the first stage
experiment.limitations: confined to the tested simulator design
experiment.conclusion: [EXP]

rows.anchor: The commissioned question is now half-answered: complexity is measurable and it reaches determination; but it has no closed form. So: N_eff is a new open mathematical item -- and unlike the others, it is a well-posed one. It joins the queue but does not displace it. The ordering stands: Factivity → Contr → ⪰.
rows.statement: Summarizes the commissioned question as half-answered (complexity is measurable and reaches determination, but has no closed form), adding N_eff to the open-item queue as a well-posed problem without displacing the standing Factivity->Contr->status-ordering research priority.

rows.anchor: CORRECTED -- the queue logic. This originally asserted that N_eff 'feeds an admissibility function that presupposes ⪰'. Not established. There are at least two independent paths: statistical admissibility (N_eff → multiplicity control → threshold), which needs no general epistemic ordering; and epistemic admissibility (N_eff → assessment → ⪰ → admissibility), which does.
rows.statement: Third explicit self-correction: retracts the claim that N_eff necessarily depends on the unresolved epistemic-status ordering, distinguishing a statistical-admissibility path (N_eff->multiplicity control->threshold, no ordering needed) from an epistemic-admissibility path (N_eff->assessment->ordering->admissibility, ordering needed) -- N_eff and the ordering are related but independent research problems until shown otherwise.

rows.anchor: One cheap item can proceed independently: require every validation step to declare its evidence channel. ... Do not formalize N_eff by adopting n(1-ρ)². It was refuted here, on a wider grid, after fitting well on a narrow one -- which is the same failure mode as the winner's curse the parent experiment measured.
rows.statement: Recommends one cheap parallel next step (require every validation step to declare its evidence channel, a schema decision not research) while explicitly forbidding adopting n(1-rho)^2 as N_eff's formalization, noting the refuted-narrow-grid-fit failure mode is structurally the same as the winner's-curse phenomenon the parent M2O experiment measured.

rows.anchor: |H| ≢ effective epistemic complexity. 1000 highly dependent hypotheses can behave like a much smaller effective hypothesis space. ... Hypothesis Space → Dependence → Effective Complexity → Evidence Burden. And importantly, we did not overfit this into a formula. The attempted closed form was rejected. That's exactly what we want from the research process.
rows.statement: Highlights the N_eff experiment's core lesson (not the specific formula) as a stable result: |H| is not equivalent to effective epistemic complexity, giving the research direction HypothesisSpace->Dependence->EffectiveComplexity->EvidenceBurden, praising the rejection of the overfit closed form as exemplary research process.

rows.anchor: Can effective hypothesis complexity be defined through distinguishability/equivalence under a regime Λ? No, not by pairwise distinguishability alone. ... H_1~_Λ H_2~_Λ...~_Λ H_12 while H_1 ≁_Λ H_12. Therefore: ~_Λ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive. Hence: H/~_Λ is not a legitimate quotient construction. That decisively kills the proposed: N_eff=|H/~_Λ|.
rows.statement: Endorses the clean mathematical negative result: a constructed chain H1~H2~...~H12 under the observational-indistinguishability relation ~_Lambda has H1 not~ H12, proving ~_Lambda is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive -- so H/~_Lambda is not a legitimate quotient and N_eff=|H/~_Lambda| is decisively refuted.

rows.anchor: Packing_δ(H) = max{|S|: S⊆H, ∀i≠j, d(H_i,H_j)>δ}. It avoids the transitivity problem. And it works remarkably well for duplicated/grouped hypotheses: 50→51.1, 200→201.9, 1000→940.6. But then: ρ=.9: Packing=1000, N_eff≈9 and ρ=.95: Packing=1000, N_eff≈4.5. So the failure is not numerical noise. It is a category error: pairwise distinguishability ≠ family-level multiplicity burden.
rows.statement: Endorses the delta-packing repair (Packing_delta(H) = max independent-set size under pairwise distance > delta) as avoiding the transitivity problem and matching grouped/duplicated cases well (50->51.1, 200->201.9, 1000->940.6), but identifies its dramatic failure under strong correlation (rho=0.9 gives Packing=1000 vs true N_eff~9; rho=0.95 gives Packing=1000 vs N_eff~4.5) as a category error: pairwise distinguishability is not the same quantity as family-level multiplicity burden.

rows.anchor: The experiment does not yet prove: 𝓗 must become (𝓗,Σ). It establishes: A set of hypotheses alone is insufficient for this particular notion of family-level burden. ... I would retain: [OPEN] A family-level epistemic object may require explicit dependence structure. rather than promote it to theory.
rows.statement: Disciplines the experiment's interpretation: it does not prove the hypothesis space must formally become (H,Sigma) with explicit dependence structure -- only that a bare hypothesis set is insufficient for this particular family-level-burden notion; records this as [OPEN], not promoted to theory.

rows.anchor: 'There appear to be at least two distinct sources of effective complexity reduction.' ... I would record it as: [PROP] At least two empirically distinguishable mechanisms appear in the tested regimes: 1. Redundancy ... 2. Coupling ... There could be: redundancy, correlation/coupling, hierarchy, geometry, common latent causes, adaptive search dependence, selection-induced dependence, temporal dependence, etc.
rows.statement: Downgrades the report's claim of 'two distinct sources of effective complexity reduction' to [PROP] 'at least two empirically distinguishable mechanisms in the tested regimes' (Redundancy and Coupling), warning against prematurely treating two observed mechanisms as an exhaustive ontology when others (hierarchy, geometry, common latent causes, adaptive-search dependence, selection-induced dependence, temporal dependence) remain possible.

rows.anchor: Identity → Distinguishability → Joint Behaviour. Level 1 -- Identity/semantic equivalence: H_i ≡_sem H_j, relevant to redundancy. Level 2 -- Pairwise distinguishability: H_i ≁_Λ H_j, a measurement property. Level 3 -- Family structure: 𝓗={H_1,...,H_n} with joint structure governing scores/evidence. This is where the experiment says pairwise equivalence is insufficient.
rows.statement: Proposes a durable three-level distinction: Level 1 Identity/semantic-equivalence (H_i=_sem H_j, relevant to redundancy), Level 2 pairwise distinguishability (H_i not~_Lambda H_j, a measurement property), Level 3 family structure (the whole collection's joint behavior) -- the KR-DIST experiment shows Level 2 constructs are insufficient to characterize Level 3.

rows.anchor: The experiment does not refute ≡_sem. ... Semantic equivalence answers something like: 'Are these two representations semantically interchangeable?' It does not necessarily answer: 'How does this entire hypothesis family behave as a joint statistical object?' Therefore: ≡_sem and family-level effective complexity should probably remain separate concepts unless future experiments establish a formal bridge.
rows.statement: Clarifies that KR-DIST does not refute semantic equivalence (=_sem) itself, only that it should not be asked to answer a question it was not designed for: =_sem answers whether two representations are semantically interchangeable, not how an entire hypothesis family behaves jointly -- the two should remain separate concepts absent a demonstrated formal bridge.

rows.anchor: 𝔥_Λ = (𝓗, ℛ_sem, Λ, Σ_Λ). But this is only a research candidate, not a proposed Theory v1.3.
rows.statement: Proposes a candidate composite object H_Lambda=(H, R_sem, Lambda, Sigma_Lambda) combining the hypothesis set, semantic-equivalence relation, evidential regime, and joint dependence structure -- explicitly only a research candidate, not a Theory v1.3 proposal.

rows.anchor: I would explicitly not let N_eff become the next central theory problem. ... We don't yet know whether effective complexity is a primitive of KnowledgeOS at all. It may turn out to be a property of a particular evidential regime, useful for statistical assessment but not part of the KnowledgeOS kernel.
rows.statement: Explicitly recommends N_eff not become the next central theory problem, since it remains unknown whether effective complexity is a KnowledgeOS primitive at all or merely a useful property of a particular evidential/statistical regime outside the kernel.

rows.anchor: | ~_Λ is not generally transitive | [NEG] | | H/~_Λ cannot generally define complexity | [NEG] | | Packing fails dramatically under strong correlation | [NEG] | | Pairwise distinguishability cannot generally measure family-level burden | [EXP/NEG] | | Semantic equivalence captures the whole N_eff problem | [NEG] | | Explicit dependence structure is required in KnowledgeOS | [OPEN] | | N_eff is a KnowledgeOS primitive | [OPEN] | | N_eff belongs in the kernel | [OPEN], currently unsupported |
rows.statement: Produces a fourteen-row status register for the KR-DIST findings, spanning [NEG] (non-transitivity, quotient invalidity, packing failure under correlation, semantic equivalence not capturing the whole N_eff problem), [EXP]/[EXP-NEG] (pairwise distinguishability insufficient for family burden), [PROP] (redundancy/coupling as distinct mechanisms, semantic equivalence capturing the redundancy component), and [OPEN] (explicit dependence structure requirement, N_eff as primitive, N_eff belonging in the kernel).

rows.anchor: Pairwise semantic/evidential distinguishability cannot carry family-level epistemic complexity by itself. And that prevents a potentially very serious theoretical mistake. So I would freeze this result, leave Theory v1.2 unchanged, and not chase another N_eff formula. ... What is the minimal joint structure required to represent family-level epistemic dependence? That is a much better question than 'what formula gives us N_eff?'
rows.statement: Ranks KR-DIST alongside the kernel-reduction and Zero experiments as among the most valuable in the programme, precisely because it discovered a boundary (pairwise distinguishability cannot carry family-level complexity) that prevents a serious theoretical mistake; recommends freezing this result, leaving v1.2 unchanged, not chasing another N_eff formula, and instead asking what minimal joint structure represents family-level epistemic dependence.

rows.anchor: FROZEN 2026-09-02 by supervisory review. Baseline v1.2, unchanged. No v1.3. no further N_eff formula hunt authorized. ... No -- not as posed. The construction fails at its first step, and the standard repair fails at its second. Two independent obstructions, and the second is the more informative.
rows.statement: The experiment result is explicitly marked FROZEN by supervisory review with an unusual explicit ban: no further N_eff formula hunt is authorized; answers the commissioned question 'no, not as posed' via two independent obstructions to defining effective complexity through distinguishability.

rows.anchor: Place 12 hypotheses with means spaced at 0.9×δ. adjacent pairs indistinguishable: true. endpoints distinguishable: true (span 3.068). H1~H2~H3~...~H12 pairwise indistinguishable; H1≁H12 endpoints distinguishable. Λ-indistinguishability is a tolerance relation, not an equivalence relation. It is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive. Therefore H/~_Λ does not exist.
rows.statement: [NEG]: constructs a 12-hypothesis sorites-chain witness (means spaced at 0.9x the resolution delta=0.3099, under regime m=40,sigma=1.0,alpha=0.05) where every adjacent pair is indistinguishable but the endpoints (span 3.068) are distinguishable -- proving Lambda-indistinguishability is a tolerance relation (reflexive, symmetric) but not transitive, so the quotient H/~_Lambda does not exist and |H/~_Lambda| cannot serve as effective complexity.

experiment.hypothesis: Λ-indistinguishability (~_Λ) is transitive, so H/~_Λ is a well-defined quotient usable as effective complexity
experiment.setup: regime Λ: m=40, sigma=1.0, alpha=0.05 giving standard error 0.1581 and resolution delta=0.3099; 12 hypotheses placed at mean spacing 0.9*delta
experiment.assumptions: pairwise indistinguishability under a standard-error-based test
experiment.inputs: 12 hypothesis means in a chain
experiment.method: test pairwise (in)distinguishability for adjacent pairs and for the chain endpoints
experiment.result: all adjacent pairs indistinguishable; endpoints distinguishable (span 3.068)
experiment.interpretation: ~_Λ is not transitive; the quotient construction fails
experiment.limitations: a direct search for a transitivity witness inside an equicorrelated (homogeneous) space found none, because uniform pairwise separation makes indistinguishability vacuously transitive there -- non-transitivity requires a range of separations
experiment.conclusion: [NEG] H/~_Λ does not exist

rows.anchor: A direct search for a transitivity witness inside the equicorrelated space returned none -- because there every pair has the same separation, so indistinguishability is all-or-nothing and vacuously transitive. Non-transitivity appears only when the space contains a range of separations, which is the general case. The homogeneous space hides the defect.
rows.statement: Notes an important methodological caveat: homogeneous (equicorrelated) hypothesis spaces hide the non-transitivity defect entirely, since uniform pairwise separation makes indistinguishability vacuously transitive there -- non-transitivity only manifests when the space contains a genuine range of separations, which is the general case.

rows.anchor: grouped 50 groups: packing 50, measured N_eff 51.1, ratio 0.98. grouped 200 groups: packing 200, N_eff 201.9, ratio 0.99. independent: packing 1000, N_eff 940.6, ratio 1.06. correlated ρ=0.5: packing 1000, N_eff 200.6, ratio 4.99. correlated ρ=0.9: packing 1000, N_eff 9.0, ratio 111. correlated ρ=0.95: packing 1000, N_eff 4.5, ratio 222. Packing matches duplication almost exactly (ratios 0.98-1.06) and fails on correlation by up to 222×.
rows.statement: [NEG]: the delta-packing number (largest pairwise-distinguishable subset, requiring no transitivity) matches measured N_eff almost exactly for duplication/grouping (ratios 0.98-1.06 across 50-group, 200-group, and fully independent spaces) but fails catastrophically under correlation, off by 111x at rho=0.9 and 222x at rho=0.95, since every pair remains individually pairwise-distinguishable (sd=0.447>delta=0.310 at rho=0.9) even though the maximum of 1000 correlated scores behaves like only ~9 independent draws.

experiment.hypothesis: The delta-packing number (largest pairwise-distinguishable subset) predicts measured N_eff across duplication and correlation regimes
experiment.setup: six hypothesis-space configurations (grouped 50/200, independent 1000, correlated rho=0.5/0.9/0.95), each with computed sd(Si-Sj), pairwise-distinguishability check, packing number, and previously measured N_eff
experiment.assumptions: delta-packing is the correct family-level generalization avoiding the transitivity problem
experiment.inputs: the six configurations
experiment.method: compute packing number per configuration and compare to previously measured N_eff (ratio)
experiment.result: ratio 0.98-1.06 for grouped/independent (duplication-type) spaces; ratio 4.99, 111, 222 for correlated spaces at rho=0.5/0.9/0.95 respectively
experiment.interpretation: packing captures redundancy/duplication but not correlation-induced coupling; multiplicity burden is driven by joint extreme-value behavior of scores, not pairwise separability
experiment.limitations: confined to the tested regime and correlation structures
experiment.conclusion: [NEG] packing fails for correlation; [EXP] burden is a joint/family property

rows.anchor: The multiplicity burden is driven by the JOINT extreme-value behaviour of the candidate scores, not by pairwise separability. A shared component moves the candidates together, so the maximum is far less extreme than 1000 independent draws would give -- while every pair stays individually resolvable. Pairwise distinguishability is the wrong invariant. It is a property of pairs; the burden is a property of the family.
rows.statement: States the substantive theoretical finding: multiplicity burden is governed by the joint extreme-value behavior of candidate scores (a shared component moves candidates together, damping the maximum below what 1000 independent draws would give) rather than by any pairwise-separability property -- pairwise distinguishability is a property of pairs, while the burden is a property of the family, making it the wrong invariant for this purpose.

rows.anchor: duplication/block structure is captured by pairwise distinguishability -- packing ≈ N_eff to within 6%. correlation/shared structure is not captured -- off by up to 222×. ... Redundancy -- candidates that are the same under the regime. ... Coupling -- candidates that are distinct but move together. This is a joint/extremal property and ≡_sem does not reach it.
rows.statement: Concludes effective complexity has at least two empirically distinct components requiring different mathematics: Redundancy (candidates identical under the regime, a pairwise/=_sem-shaped notion, matched to within 6% by packing) and Coupling (candidates distinct but moving together jointly, a joint/extremal property that =_sem does not reach, off by up to 222x under packing) -- 'at least' is explicitly load-bearing since these need not be exhaustive or ontologically distinct.

rows.anchor: This does NOT refute ≡_sem. It shows only that ≡_sem must not be asked to do a job it was never designed for. ... ≡_sem and family-level effective complexity should remain separate concepts unless a future experiment establishes a formal bridge -- which is a good outcome, because it prevents forcing everything into one equivalence relation.
rows.statement: Clarifies semantic equivalence (=_sem) is not refuted by this experiment, only shown to answer a narrower question ('are two representations semantically interchangeable') than family-level joint behavior; =_sem and family-level effective complexity should remain separate concepts pending a demonstrated formal bridge -- judged a good outcome since it prevents forcing everything into one equivalence relation.

rows.anchor: 1 Identity/semantic equivalence H_i≡_sem H_j -- redundancy. 2 Pairwise distinguishability H_i≁_Λ H_j -- a measurement property. 3 Family structure -- how does the whole collection behave jointly? -- coupling, where levels 1-2 are insufficient. 𝔥_Λ = (𝓗, ℛ_sem, Λ, Σ_Λ) -- a research candidate, not a proposed Theory v1.3.
rows.statement: Formally states the three-level distinction (Identity/semantic-equivalence for redundancy; pairwise distinguishability as a measurement property; family structure for coupling, where the first two levels are insufficient) and the candidate composite object H_Lambda=(H, R_sem, Lambda, Sigma_Lambda), explicitly only a research candidate.

rows.anchor: Do not run a third formula hunt. Two have now failed for the same underlying reason: n(1-ρ)² (fitted, then refuted on a wider grid) and packing (structural, but pairwise). ... Is the coupling component expressible at all in the vocabulary of hypothesis equivalence -- or does it require an explicitly joint object (a covariance/dependence structure carried alongside the hypothesis set)?
rows.statement: Explicitly bans a third N_eff formula hunt, noting two attempts (n(1-rho)^2, refuted on a wider grid; packing, structurally sound but pairwise) have now failed for the same underlying reason (both are pairwise/local, but the burden is a joint/family property); reframes the next question as whether the coupling component is expressible in the vocabulary of hypothesis equivalence at all, or requires an explicitly joint dependence-structure object.

rows.anchor: Scope corrected. This originally read 'a hypothesis space ... is not a set but a structured family (𝓗,Σ).' Too strong -- the experiment does not establish that. What it establishes is: [EXP] A set of hypotheses alone is insufficient for this particular notion of family-level burden. ... Recorded as: [OPEN] A family-level epistemic object may require explicit dependence structure.
rows.statement: Explicit self-correction: walks back an original overclaim (hypothesis space 'is not a set but a structured family (H,Sigma)') to the narrower established fact (a bare hypothesis set is insufficient for this particular family-level-burden notion), recording the stronger claim only as [OPEN].

rows.anchor: N_eff must NOT become the next central theory problem. We do not yet know whether effective complexity is a KnowledgeOS primitive at all -- it may be a property of a particular evidential regime, useful for statistical assessment and outside the kernel. ... Do not put statistical mechanisms into the kernel merely because KnowledgeOS can use them.
rows.statement: Reaffirms N_eff must not become the central theory problem, since it is unknown whether effective complexity is a KnowledgeOS kernel primitive at all versus a property of a particular evidential regime; restates the general kernel-discipline principle against putting useful statistical mechanisms (candidate generation, selection, multiplicity control, correlation modelling, validation, Bayesian updating) into the kernel merely because they are useful capabilities.

rows.anchor: Pairwise semantic/evidential distinguishability cannot carry family-level epistemic complexity by itself. ... I would interpret 'by itself' as load-bearing. The experiment does not establish ¬∃F(~_Λ) in every conceivable mathematical construction. It establishes ... pairwise distinguishability alone ⇏ adequate representation of family-level burden under the tested constructions/regimes.
rows.statement: Tightens the frozen central claim by treating 'by itself' as load-bearing: the experiment does not prove no function of pairwise distinguishability could ever work in any construction, only that pairwise distinguishability alone does not adequately represent family-level burden under the specific tested constructions and regimes.

rows.anchor: I would investigate: H_i ~_Λ H_j where Λ specifies the relevant observation/evidence regime. Then potentially: H/~_Λ becomes the mathematically meaningful space of distinguishable alternatives. That is much deeper than simply counting candidates.
rows.statement: Proposes investigating a hypothesis-indistinguishability relation H_i~_Lambda H_j (regime-specific) with H/~_Lambda as the mathematically meaningful space of distinguishable alternatives -- this specific construction is the one KR-DIST (S2471) tests and refutes via a non-transitivity counterexample.

rows.anchor: grouped g=200: measured 201.9, participation ratio 200.0. grouped g=50: measured 51.1, participation ratio 50.0. equicorr ρ=0.5: measured 200.6, participation ratio 4.0. equicorr ρ=0.9: measured 9.0, participation ratio 1.2. All four are exact on block structure (200→200, 50→50) and all four fail on equicorrelation.
rows.statement: [NEG] H7: tests four spectral functionals (participation ratio, exp(spectral entropy), trace/lambda_max, rank) against measured N_eff across seven spaces; all four are exact on block/grouped structure (200->200, 50->50) but all fail dramatically under equicorrelation (e.g. participation ratio gives 4.0 vs measured 200.6 at rho=0.5, mean |log ratio| error 0.497 to 1.797 across the four functionals).

experiment.hypothesis: H7: a spectral functional (e.g. participation ratio) of the Hilbert representation represents effective hypothesis complexity
experiment.setup: compute four spectral functionals (participation ratio, exp(spectral entropy), trace/lambda_max, rank) for seven hypothesis-space configurations with known measured N_eff from KR-NEFF
experiment.assumptions: the covariance spectrum is the relevant Hilbert-space object
experiment.inputs: independent n=1000, grouped g=200, grouped g=50, equicorrelated rho=0.1/0.5/0.9/0.95
experiment.method: compute each spectral functional per space and compare to measured N_eff
experiment.result: exact match on block/grouped spaces; all four functionals fail on equicorrelated spaces, with errors up to nearly 2 orders of magnitude in log-ratio
experiment.interpretation: spectral functionals capture redundancy/duplication exactly but not correlation-induced coupling
experiment.limitations: confined to tested functionals and correlation structures
experiment.conclusion: [NEG] H7 refuted for the tested spectral functionals

rows.anchor: pairwise -- δ-packing (FR-001): at ρ=0.5, measured 200.6 -- 1000, over by 5×, worst case 222× at ρ=0.95. spectral -- participation ratio (here): 4.0, under by 50×, worst case 50×. The measured family-level burden is captured by neither construction, and the two err in opposite directions.
rows.statement: [EXP], the central new finding: comparing FR-001's pairwise delta-packing (which overestimates burden, up to 222x at rho=0.95) against KR-HILBERT's spectral participation ratio (which underestimates, up to 50x) shows the two independent mathematical routes bracket the true measured burden from opposite directions, with neither capturing it -- 1000 (pairwise) > 200.6 (measured) > 4.0 (spectral) at rho=0.5.

rows.anchor: CORRECTED -- do not freeze 'the answer lies between them'. An earlier wording said the burden 'lies BETWEEN' the two constructions. That is not a mathematical result and must not be frozen as one. ... What is supported is the weaker, precise statement: [EXP] Under the tested correlation-family regimes, the measured effective multiplicity burden is not represented by pairwise δ-packing, and is not represented by the tested standard spectral functionals.
rows.statement: Explicit self-correction: retracts an overclaimed 'the answer lies between the two constructions' (which presupposes an ordering and containment proof that do not exist) to the weaker, precise statement that under the tested regimes the burden is represented by neither pairwise delta-packing nor the tested standard spectral functionals -- the directional observation (pairwise over, spectral under) is recorded as a structural boundary, not an interval claim.

rows.anchor: The participation ratio measures the effective dimension of the covariance -- how many directions carry variance. The multiplicity burden measures the effective number of independent extreme-value draws -- a property of the tail of the maximum. These are different functionals of the same spectrum, and protocol §4 was right to forbid their identification.
rows.statement: Explains why participation ratio and multiplicity burden diverge: the former measures effective covariance dimension (how many directions carry variance) while the latter is a tail-of-the-maximum extreme-value property -- distinct functionals of the same spectrum, confirming the protocol's explicit prohibition on identifying participation ratio with effective hypothesis complexity.

rows.anchor: N_eff = 1 / Σ_i |⟨K_t,e_i⟩|^4. The effective number of hypotheses is the inverse of the participation ratio. This solves: The multiplicity penalty problem, The evidence burden problem, The candidate count vs diversity problem.
rows.statement: Proposes the explicit inverse-participation-ratio formula N_eff=1/sum_i|<K_t,e_i>|^4 as solving the multiplicity/evidence-burden/diversity problems -- this exact functional (participation ratio) is subsequently tested and refuted in S2476's H7 (exact on block structure, but off by up to 50x under equicorrelation).

rows.anchor: 6. **N_eff permanently off the critical path** — Per FR-001
rows.statement: Restates the FR-001 governance consequence that N_eff (effective hypothesis complexity) is permanently off the critical path for kernel selection.

rows.anchor: **Two things to keep separate, on review instruction:** `N_eff` and `⪰` are **independent** research problems — the claim that `N_eff` presupposes `⪰` is **not established**
rows.statement: Records a review instruction that N_eff and ⪰ (progress ordering) must be kept as independent research problems; the claim that N_eff presupposes ⪰ is not established, and ≡_sem is not refuted and must not be asked a question it was not designed for.

lexical.anchor: |H|=1000 while changing dependence structure. It obtains approximately: N_eff≈940.6, 201.9, 51.1, 9.0 for increasingly dependent spaces. ... |H|=1000, 50 groups versus |H|=50, 50 independent candidates. They produce essentially identical threshold behavior and N_eff. ... |H| is not an adequate measure of hypothesis-space complexity.

formal.anchor: What equivalence relation on hypotheses makes two candidate spaces epistemically equivalent? ... H_i ~_Λ H_j iff they are indistinguishable with respect to the observables relevant to Λ. Then: H/~_Λ gives equivalence classes. A first approximation to effective complexity could then be related to: |H/~_Λ|. But do not adopt this as N_eff. It is a research direction.

governance.anchor: Do not add candidate_count to Theory v1.2. Do not add N_eff=n(1-ρ)^2. Do not promote N_eff to a canonical KnowledgeOS primitive. Do not modify v1.2 yet.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Candidate Space → Multiplicity → Dependence Structure → Effective Complexity → Evidence Burden → Assessment → Validation → Determination. But the mathematical definition of Effective Complexity remains open. ... I suspect these two research lines will eventually meet at: semantic equivalence / indistinguishability.
rationale_evidence.statement: Updates the research map to Candidate Space->Multiplicity->Dependence Structure->Effective Complexity->Evidence Burden->Assessment->Validation->Determination, with Effective Complexity's mathematical definition left open, and hypothesizes this line and the Structure->Projection->Information Loss->Invariant Preservation line will eventually converge at semantic equivalence/indistinguishability -- 'how many genuinely distinguishable alternatives does the epistemic system actually have?' as a deeper question than raw hypothesis count.

aliases: Truth, Validity, Belief, Knowledge and Epistemic Status

sources.note: S0906's Step 25O: separates world truth from KnowledgeOS's governed epistemic acceptance across five truth regimes, building on but distinct from prior evidence/assessment/status objects (evidence-assessment-algebra, epistemic-acceptance-commitment from B0021).

rows.anchor: Truth(A,W_t) ... KnowledgeOS generally does not have direct access to W_t ... Truth\neq Evidence\neq Knowledge
rows.statement: States the fundamental separation: Truth(A,W_t) asks whether A is actually true in the world, but KnowledgeOS only has observations O and evidence E, not direct world access — Truth ≠ Evidence ≠ Knowledge.

rows.anchor: Truth(A,W_t)? Support(A,K_t)? Accepted(A,K_t)? Sufficient(A,D,C)? These are not equivalent
rows.statement: Distinguishes four separate questions for any assertion A: is it actually true, do we have supporting evidence, does the system currently accept it as knowledge, and is it sufficiently established for a particular decision — explicitly not equivalent.

rows.anchor: Truth(A,W)=True while Known(A,K)=False ... Truth does not depend on whether KnowledgeOS knows it
rows.statement: Worked example: before KnowledgeOS receives evidence, the world can already be true — Truth(A,W)=True while Known(A,K)=False — 'truth does not depend on whether KnowledgeOS knows it.'

rows.anchor: Truth(A,W)=False yet Support(A,K)=Strong ... Strongly supported knowledge can still be false ... not a defect ... an unavoidable property of finite, fallible observation
rows.statement: Worked reverse example: an erroneous database record can produce Support(A,K)=Strong while Truth(A,W)=False — 'strongly supported knowledge can still be false,' explicitly not a model defect but an unavoidable property of finite, fallible observation.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS knowledge is an assertion that has passed the applicable evidence, semantic, temporal and governance criteria ... Knowledge=GovernedAcceptance, not Knowledge=TrueWorldTruth
rows.statement: Redefines KnowledgeOS knowledge operationally rather than metaphysically: Knowledge=GovernedAcceptance, not Knowledge=TrueWorldTruth — 'a crucial distinction.'

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS\rightarrow Evidence\rightarrow Assessment\rightarrow Acceptance ... does not magically obtain omniscient access to W
rows.statement: States Truth(A,W) remains an external semantic target KnowledgeOS cannot directly calculate; instead it follows Evidence->Assessment->Acceptance, estimating epistemic status rather than obtaining omniscient world access.

rows.anchor: 2+2=4 ... version string matches regex ... ValidFrom\le t<ValidUntil ... Some truths are computable; world truth in general is not
rows.statement: Gives three examples of directly computable truth (arithmetic, regex matching, validity-interval evaluation), concluding 'some truths are computable; world truth in general is not.'

rows.anchor: LogicalTruth(A) from EmpiricalTruth(A,W) ... P\lor\neg P ... Nexus is currently running 3.70
rows.statement: Distinguishes LogicalTruth(A) (e.g. the tautology P∨¬P under classical logic) from EmpiricalTruth(A,W) (e.g. an empirical version claim) as established by different mechanisms.

rows.anchor: DomainTruth ... a production deployment requires Architecture Board approval ... Truth_{domain}(A,\Omega) may be evaluated from GovernanceRules ... not the same as empirical world truth
rows.statement: Introduces DomainTruth: a governance policy statement is true within an organizational governance model if authoritative — Truth_domain(A,Omega) evaluated from GovernanceRules, distinct from empirical world truth.

rows.anchor: Truth_{math}(A,\mathcal M) ... Axioms+Definitions+InferenceRules ... Logical/Mathematical, Empirical/World, Domain/Governance
rows.statement: Adds Truth_math(A,M) (a theorem true relative to axioms+definitions+inference rules), giving three named truth regimes: Logical/Mathematical, Empirical/World, Domain/Governance — KnowledgeOS should know which regime applies.

rows.anchor: TruthContext=(Domain,Model,Axioms,ReferenceTime) ... Without a context, true may be underspecified
rows.statement: Defines TruthContext=(Domain,Model,Axioms,ReferenceTime), making Truth(A,TruthContext) meaningful — without context, 'true' may be underspecified.

rows.anchor: Belief(A) ... a human can believe A while Truth(A)=False ... an AI can assign P(A)=0.9 while A is false ... Belief\neq Truth
rows.statement: Introduces Belief(A) as a proposition held with epistemic weight, distinct from truth (a human or an AI can believe/assign high probability to a false proposition) — Belief ≠ Truth; recommends using the term Assessment(A) instead of 'belief' to avoid anthropomorphic confusion.

rows.anchor: P(A\mid E)=0.95 ... does not mean Truth(A)=0.95 ... Probability measures uncertainty; truth is not a confidence score
rows.statement: Clarifies that a probability P(A|E)=0.95 is a model-relative uncertainty measure, not Truth(A)=0.95 — 'truth is not a percentage... probability measures uncertainty; truth is not a confidence score.'

rows.anchor: Supported, Refuted, Unknown, Conflicted ... epistemic statuses, not truth values
rows.statement: Proposes a four-value practical epistemic-status space {Supported, Refuted, Unknown, Conflicted}, explicitly labeled epistemic statuses, not truth values.

rows.anchor: Status(A)=Unknown ... must not infer Status(A)=False ... Unknown\neq False ... one of the most important rules in the entire architecture
rows.statement: States the central rule Unknown ≠ False — no-evidence must not be inferred as False — called 'one of the most important rules in the entire architecture.'

rows.anchor: AbsenceOfEvidence(A)\not\Rightarrow\neg A ... unless the domain explicitly defines a closed-world assumption
rows.statement: States the open-world default: absence of evidence does not imply ¬A unless a domain explicitly adopts a closed-world assumption; illustrated with 'no approved architecture record found' justifying only NoApprovedRecordFound, not ArchitectureNotApproved.

rows.anchor: ClosedWorldAssumption ... a domain rule, not a universal law ... Open/Closed World = Explicit Domain Semantics
rows.statement: Illustrates closed-world reasoning as legitimate only when explicitly adopted (e.g. a registry table where absence implies non-existence) — 'a domain rule, not a universal law': Open/Closed World = Explicit Domain Semantics.

rows.anchor: Firewall rule exists ... Zero should contain MissingEvidence(FirewallRule), not FirewallRule=False ... exactly the behavior we want
rows.statement: Reapplies Unknown≠False to Zero: a missing-evidence requirement should register as MissingEvidence(FirewallRule), not FirewallRule=False, letting Lord choose to inspect rather than assume failure.

rows.anchor: Accept(A,E,C,M) ... Accepted(A)=EvidenceSufficient\land ContextCorrect\land TemporalValidity\land NoBlockingConflict\land GovernanceSatisfied
rows.statement: Defines the governed acceptance function Accept(A,E,C,M) as a conjunction of five criteria (EvidenceSufficient, ContextCorrect, TemporalValidity, NoBlockingConflict, GovernanceSatisfied), deterministic if all constituent models are deterministic.

type_signature.domain: Assertion x Evidence x Context x Model

rows.anchor: Accepted(A)\not\Rightarrow Truth(A,W) ... KnowledgeOS is justified in treating A as accepted knowledge under its current model ... a much more defensible claim
rows.statement: States 'perhaps the most important equation of 25O': Accepted(A) does not imply Truth(A,W) — acceptance only means KnowledgeOS is justified in treating A as accepted under its current model, 'a much more defensible claim.'

rows.anchor: Truth(A,W)\not\Rightarrow Accepted(A) ... the server really runs 3.70, but KnowledgeOS has not observed it
rows.statement: States the converse non-implication: Truth(A,W) does not imply Accepted(A) — an assertion can be true but unobserved/unknown.

rows.anchor: | World truth | KnowledgeOS acceptance | Interpretation | ... The third case is unavoidable in any empirical knowledge system
rows.statement: Presents a four-quadrant table crossing World truth (True/False) with KnowledgeOS acceptance (Yes/No): correctly known; true but unknown; false belief/incorrect knowledge; correctly not accepted — the false-but-accepted quadrant is 'unavoidable in any empirical knowledge system.'

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS=Oracle ... KnowledgeOS=Governed epistemic system ... evidence quality; provenance; calibration; reproducibility; revision behavior; error detection; conflict handling
rows.statement: Argues the architecture does not promise KnowledgeOS=Oracle but KnowledgeOS=Governed epistemic system, measured by evidence quality, provenance, calibration, reproducibility, revision behavior, error detection, and conflict handling — 'much more scientifically defensible.'

rows.anchor: WorldStatus(A) from EpistemicStatus(A,K) ... KnowledgeOS computes epistemic status, not omniscient world truth
rows.statement: Proposes explicitly separating WorldStatus(A) (generally inaccessible) from EpistemicStatus(A,K) (what KnowledgeOS computes) — 'KnowledgeOS computes epistemic status, not omniscient world truth.'

rows.anchor: Lord identifies Zero=NeedDirectObservation ... Knowledge is strengthened through observation, not through confidence inflation
rows.statement: When EpistemicStatus(A)=Unknown, Lord can select an observation action to potentially establish Accepted(A) — 'knowledge is strengthened through observation, not through confidence inflation.'

rows.anchor: inspect the server at t=10:00 ... does not establish Nexus=3.70 for all future times ... assertion must include temporal scope A(t)
rows.statement: Notes that verifying a fact at one time does not establish it for all future times, requiring assertions to carry explicit temporal scope A(t) — 'connects 25O directly to our temporal model.'

rows.anchor: Nexus=3.70 true for ProductionServer_X, false for DevelopmentServer_Y ... Context is part of knowledge identity
rows.statement: Worked example reaffirming Context is part of knowledge identity: the same version assertion can be true for one server and false for another depending on subject/context.

rows.anchor: Valid(A,t,C,M) ... distinct from Truth(A,W_t) ... Valid(A,2025)=True while Valid(A,2026)=False ... Expired/obsolete\neq False
rows.statement: Defines Valid(A,t,C,M) — applicability under temporal/contextual/model conditions — distinct from Truth(A,W_t); worked example of validity changing across years due to an upgrade, restating Expired/obsolete ≠ False.

rows.anchor: Migration is approved ... ApprovalEvent ... ApprovedByAuthority(A) ... does not imply MigrationIsTechnicallySafe ... GovernanceTruth\neq TechnicalTruth
rows.statement: Introduces GovernanceTruth as an organizational fact established by an authoritative ApprovalEvent (ApprovedByAuthority(A)), explicitly not implying technical safety — GovernanceTruth ≠ TechnicalTruth, 'both may be required for Sarathi.'

rows.anchor: TechnicalAssessment=Safe but GovernanceApproval=False \Rightarrow DecisionExecutable=False ... Conversely GovernanceApproval=True but TechnicalAssessment=Unsafe \Rightarrow DecisionExecutable=False
rows.statement: Worked two-branch example showing both technical safety and governance approval are independently necessary for DecisionExecutable=True — 'authorization and technical justification are separate dimensions.'

rows.anchor: Truth(A)=True ... there may be no action ... Truth\rightarrow Knowledge\rightarrow Decision\rightarrow Authorization\rightarrow Action ... separate transitions
rows.statement: States truth does not automatically imply action: KnowledgeOS must keep Truth->Knowledge->Decision->Authorization->Action as separate transitions.

rows.anchor: EpistemicStatus=(Support,Conflict,Validity,Freshness,Authority,Uncertainty) ... much richer than true or confidence=0.91
rows.statement: Proposes a six-dimension EpistemicStatus tuple (Support, Conflict, Validity, Freshness, Authority, Uncertainty) with a worked instantiation, contrasted as 'much richer' than a bare boolean or scalar confidence.

rows.anchor: Assessment(A)=(Prior,LikelihoodModel,Evidence,Posterior,Sensitivity) for probabilistic ... (Rules,Inputs,Derivation,Validation) for deterministic ... (Axioms,Definitions,Proof,ProofChecker) for theorems ... Proven(A) has a different meaning from Supported(A)
rows.statement: Defines three distinct typed Assessment structures for probabilistic, deterministic-rule, and mathematical-theorem assertions, noting Proven(A) has a different meaning from Supported(A) — 'another reason not to use one universal Boolean truth field.'

rows.anchor: TruthRegime=\{Mathematical,Logical,Empirical,Domain,Governance\} ... each regime has different validation semantics
rows.statement: Formalizes a five-value TruthRegime enum {Mathematical, Logical, Empirical, Domain, Governance}, each with different validation semantics — 'very important for a general KnowledgeOS.'

rows.anchor: Can one assertion belong to multiple regimes? Yes ... a governance rule; a formal organizational policy; represented logically; empirically checked against records ... each derivation should identify its basis
rows.statement: Notes one proposition (e.g. an approval-requirement policy) can simultaneously participate in multiple truth regimes (governance, logical, empirical) — each derivation should identify its own basis.

rows.anchor: Basis(A) ... empirical_observation / governance_policy / formal_derivation / probabilistic_inference ... makes reasoning auditable
rows.statement: Requires assertions to record Basis(A) (e.g. empirical_observation, governance_policy, formal_derivation, probabilistic_inference), making reasoning auditable.

rows.anchor: is_true BOOLEAN ... strongly recommend against ... Unknown would become False. Supported would become True. Both are wrong
rows.statement: Strongly warns against a single universal is_true boolean field as the central knowledge representation since it would collapse Unknown into False and Supported into True — 'both are wrong' — recommends EpistemicStatus plus, where applicable, a regime-explicit TruthAssessment.

rows.anchor: Test A true but unknown ... EpistemicStatus=Unknown. PASS. Test B false but believed ... EpistemicStatus=Supported, later Refuted. PASS. Test C no evidence -> Unknown not False. PASS. Test D strong evidence -> StrongSupport not Truth=True. PASS. Test E governance approval -> GovernanceStatus=Approve
rows.statement: Runs six falsification tests (A-F), all PASS: (A) true-in-world-but-no-evidence yields EpistemicStatus=Unknown; (B) false-in-world-but-bad-evidence yields Supported now, with later revision able to produce Refuted; (C) no evidence yields Unknown, never False; (D) strong evidence yields StrongSupport, not an automatic Truth=True claim; (E) governance approval yields GovernanceStatus=Approved without implying TechnicalSafety=True; (F) a proof-checker-established mathematical theorem yields Proven, distinct from empirical-observation-based Supported.

experiment.hypothesis: The Truth/Support/Acceptance/regime distinctions behave correctly across six representative scenarios.
experiment.setup: Six scenarios (A-F) spanning true-unknown, false-believed, no-evidence, strong-evidence, governance-approval, and mathematical-proof cases.
experiment.assumptions: n/a
experiment.inputs: n/a
experiment.method: apply EpistemicStatus/Accepted/regime definitions to each scenario
experiment.result: All six scenarios produce the theoretically expected, non-conflated status
experiment.interpretation: Confirms the Truth!=Evidence!=Knowledge!=Belief!=Probability separation holds across varied cases.
experiment.limitations: illustrative, not executed
experiment.conclusion: All six tests PASS.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS does not need to solve ... what is absolute truth? ... needs to solve the engineering problem ... computationally tractable to a very large extent
rows.statement: States the deeper result: KnowledgeOS reframes the unsolved philosophical problem of absolute truth into the tractable engineering problem of what epistemic status a proposition can legitimately be assigned given evidence/context/model/governance.

rows.statement: Step 25O self-verdict: PASS, with four boxed central invariants: EpistemicAcceptance ≠ WorldTruth; Unknown ≠ False; Evidence ≠ Truth; Probability ≠ Truth.

rows.anchor: Evidence Algebra, Knowledge Identity, Knowledge State Algebra, Revision Algebra, Distributed Merge, Decision Algebra, Epistemic Status ... the remaining question is becoming narrower
rows.statement: Summarizes seven established sub-theories so far (Evidence Algebra, Knowledge Identity, Knowledge State Algebra, Revision Algebra, Distributed Merge, Decision Algebra, Epistemic Status), noting the remaining question is narrowing.

rows.statement: Closes by posing causality as the next challenge (worked example: Nexus upgrade -> configuration change -> service outage), distinguishing TemporalSequence from Causation, and transitioning to Step 25P (Causality, Counterfactuals, Interventions and Root-Cause Knowledge) rather than the step-numerically-next 25N — a continuation of this batch's numeric step-order deviation (S0906/Step-25O precedes S0907/Step-25N in file order).
