aliases: Step 23: Epistemic Sufficiency, Readiness, Completeness, and the Knowledge Boundary

sources.note: S0881's Step 23, revisiting the sufficiency/readiness/completeness theme first opened in Step 13 (S0867) with much heavier mathematical formalization: the EpistemicContract as the Knowledge-to-Action bridge, three separated readiness levels, Knowledge Boundary/Frontier, EpistemicGap and Epistemic Debt, KnowledgeOS Goal=max Utility(K,P) not max|K|, and S1-S16 invariants; this file's own closing section proposes Step 24, which the batch already processed as S0880.

rows.anchor: When is the knowledge we have sufficient for the purpose for which we want to use it? The answer cannot be: When the LLM is confident. Nor: When we have enough documents. Nor: When the probability is above 95%. Sufficiency is always relative to a purpose.
rows.statement: States the governing principle that sufficiency is always relative to a purpose, rejecting three naive substitutes (LLM confidence, document quantity, probability threshold).

rows.anchor:
We must separate four concepts: Knowledge 
eq Completeness 
eq Sufficiency 
eq Readiness. A knowledge state may be incomplete but sufficient. Conversely, it may contain enormous amounts of information but still be insufficient.
rows.statement: States the four-way separation Knowledge≠Completeness≠Sufficiency≠Readiness — incomplete knowledge can be sufficient, and voluminous knowledge can still be insufficient.

rows.anchor: Example ... version = 3.69, host = nexus3.dgverlag.de. This may be sufficient to answer What Nexus version is installed? But it is not necessarily sufficient to answer Can we safely migrate Nexus tomorrow? ... dependencies; backup status; network connectivity; certificates; storage; target environme
rows.statement: Illustrates purpose-relative sufficiency with a Nexus example: version/host is sufficient for a version query but not for a migration-safety question requiring ten additional dependencies.

rows.anchor: Knowledge sufficiency is a relation ... Sufficient(K,P,C,t) ... This is not simply a property of K. ... Purpose is essential ... Sufficient(K,P_1)=True for AnswerQuestion but Sufficient(K,P_2)=False for AuthorizeProductionChange. There is no universally sufficient knowledge state.
rows.statement: Defines Sufficient(K,P,C,t) as a relation (not a property of K alone), showing the same K can be sufficient for one purpose and insufficient for another — no universally sufficient knowledge state.

rows.anchor: Completeness ... Coverage(K,P) = |SatisfiedRequirements|/|\mathcal R(P)|. Coverage\neq Sufficiency. ... Why completeness is not enough ... Coverage=99%. But the missing 1% is: Production backup verification. Then the knowledge may still be NotReady. Thus a weighted requirement model is more appropri
rows.statement: Defines Coverage(K,P) as satisfied-requirement fraction, distinct from Sufficiency, illustrated by 99% coverage still being NotReady if the missing 1% is the critical backup-verification requirement.

rows.anchor: Critical requirements ... Criticality(r_i). MissingCriticalRequirement \Rightarrow NotReady for purposes where that requirement is mandatory. ... Knowledge requirements ... R(P)=\{R_1,\ldots,R_n\} ... R1: Current version known ... R7: Authorization established. Now readiness becomes computable. ...
rows.statement: Defines Criticality(r_i) forcing NotReady on any missing critical requirement, a seven-item worked migration requirement set R(P), and a five-value Status enum {Satisfied,Unsatisfied,Unknown,Conflicted,NotApplicable} richer than a boolean.

rows.anchor: Readiness ... Ready(K,P) = the knowledge state contains sufficient validated information to perform the purpose P under the applicable rules and constraints. Ready(K,P) = \bigwedge_{r_i\in R_{hard}(P)} Satisfied(K,r_i) plus NoCriticalConflict and ApplicableGovernance. ... Readiness is not confidence
rows.statement: Defines Ready(K,P) as a conjunction over all hard requirements plus no-critical-conflict and applicable-governance conditions, stating HighConfidenceInOneAssertion ≠ DecisionReadiness — one strongly-confirmed fact does not make the whole knowledge state ready.

rows.anchor: Readiness is purpose-dependent ... For P_1=Inventory one trusted observation may be sufficient. For P_2=MigrationAuthorization we may require independent confirmation; current timestamp; system-of-record evidence. EvidenceRequirement(A,P_1)\neq EvidenceRequirement(A,P_2).
rows.statement: Shows the same assertion's required evidence strength differs by purpose (inventory query vs migration authorization) — EvidenceRequirement(A,P1)≠EvidenceRequirement(A,P2).

rows.anchor: Epistemic contract ... EpistemicContract as a first-class domain concept. What must be known, at what strength, from what authority, for what purpose? EC=(Purpose,Requirements,EvidenceRules,UncertaintyLimits,ConflictRules,TemporalRules,AuthorityRules). ... This is a major architectural concept ... T
rows.statement: Defines EpistemicContract EC=(Purpose,Requirements,EvidenceRules,UncertaintyLimits,ConflictRules,TemporalRules,AuthorityRules) as the bridge between Knowledge and Action, turning sufficiency from subjective into computable evaluation.

rows.anchor: Example: answering a factual question ... R_1=VersionKnown, R_2=CurrentnessVerified both Satisfied. Then Ready=True. ... Example: production migration ... Version, Backup, Dependencies, Target, Rollback, Authorization, ChangeWindow. Rollback=Unknown. Therefore Ready=False. KnowledgeOS should not exe
rows.statement: Works two contrasting Epistemic Contract evaluations: a simple version query (both requirements satisfied, Ready=True) and a migration (one Unknown requirement — Rollback — forces Ready=False).

rows.anchor: Zero's new role ... Zero can compare Requirements(P) against Knowledge(K). Then generate EpistemicDiscrepancy such as: Rollback capability is not established. This is different from an ordinary domain discrepancy. ... Lord's new role ... What action would close this epistemic gap? a_1=VerifyRollback
rows.statement: Extends Zero to produce an EpistemicDiscrepancy (distinct from an ordinary domain discrepancy) when requirements aren't met, and Lord to propose InformationAction closing it, a major architecture extension.

rows.anchor: Information actions ... An action does not necessarily modify the business/system state. It may modify KnowledgeState. QueryDatabase, InspectConfiguration, InterviewExpert, RunTest, RetrieveDocument. These are EpistemicActions. ... Two kinds of action ... World-changing action Action_W:S\rightarrow
rows.statement: Defines EpistemicActions (five examples) modifying KnowledgeState without necessarily changing the world, distinguishing World-changing Action_W:S→S' from Knowledge-changing Action_K:K→K' (with some actions doing both, e.g. running a migration test).

rows.anchor: This gives us two state spaces ... WorldState and KnowledgeState. They evolve differently. S_{t+1}=T_S(S_t,e_t) and K_{t+1}=T_K(K_t,o_t,e_t). This distinction is fundamental. ... Knowledge is not reality ... K_t\neq S_t. KnowledgeOS represents beliefs/commitments about reality. It does not become re
rows.statement: Reaffirms K_t≠S_t (WorldState and KnowledgeState as two separately evolving spaces), explicitly connecting this to an earlier 'Knowledge Atma' philosophical discussion — the enduring knowledge-bearing identity/state structure must never be confused with the external world it models.

rows.anchor: Knowledge lag ... S_t\neq K_t. There may be a lag: ObservationLatency between RealityChange and KnowledgeUpdate. ... Staleness ... Freshness(A,t_2) must be evaluated. This connects Step 23 directly to Step 16. ... Temporal sufficiency ... A backup was verified six months ago. might be sufficient for
rows.statement: Defines ObservationLatency between reality change and knowledge update, requiring Freshness(A,t) evaluation and a TemporalRequirement(P) in the Epistemic Contract — the same evidence can be sufficient for historical documentation but not for an imminent migration.

rows.anchor: Evidence freshness ... Age(e,t)=t-Timestamp(e). Age(e,t)\leq \tau_P. \tau_P=24h. Again, \tau_P is a policy parameter, not a universal constant.
rows.statement: Defines evidence Age(e,t)=t-Timestamp(e) with a policy-specific freshness threshold τ_P, never a universal constant.

rows.anchor: Completeness as requirement coverage ... Coverage(K,P) = \sum_i w_i Satisfied_i / \sum_i w_i. This is useful for reporting. But readiness should still enforce hard constraints separately. ... Weighted completeness ... Coverage=0.93. reported as 93% of the assessed knowledge requirements are satisfie
rows.statement: Defines weighted Coverage as useful for reporting only, warning it must never be automatically taken as Ready=True — hard constraints are enforced separately.

rows.anchor: Readiness as a predicate ... Ready(K,P) = HardSatisfied \land CriticalUncertaintyAcceptable \land ConflictAcceptable \land TemporalValid \land AuthoritySatisfied. This is much more robust.
rows.statement: Defines the robust Ready(K,P) predicate as a five-way conjunction (HardSatisfied, CriticalUncertaintyAcceptable, ConflictAcceptable, TemporalValid, AuthoritySatisfied).

rows.anchor: Three readiness levels ... ReadyForInformation, ReadyForDecision, ReadyForExecution. These should be separate. ... Information-ready ... sufficient evidence to provide an answer within the requested scope. It does not imply decision readiness. ... Decision-ready ... sufficient knowledge to evaluate
rows.statement: Defines three separated readiness levels (ReadyForInformation, ReadyForDecision, ReadyForExecution) with ExecutionReady⇒DecisionReady (but not the converse), each not implying the next.

rows.anchor: Authorization-ready versus execution-ready ... A decision can be authorized while an infrastructure prerequisite remains missing. Authorization\neq OperationalReadiness.
rows.statement: States Authorization ≠ OperationalReadiness — a decision can be authorized while an infrastructure prerequisite remains unmet.

rows.anchor: Knowledge boundary ... B(K,P) as the boundary between what KnowledgeOS can currently establish for purpose P and what remains outside its justified knowledge. B=\{x\mid x\ is\ relevant \land not\ sufficiently\ established\}. ... The boundary is valuable ... We know X. We have evidence for Y. Z is pl
rows.statement: Defines the Knowledge Boundary B(K,P) (relevant-but-not-sufficiently-established items), valuable for honestly distinguishing known/evidenced/plausible/unknown/disputed/undeterminable rather than producing an answer everywhere.

rows.anchor: Knowledge frontier ... F(K,P) as the frontier between established knowledge and unresolved requirements. Known ├── Nexus identity ... Frontier ├── Backup validity ├── Rollback capability └── Target capacity. The frontier tells Lord where to investigate next.
rows.statement: Defines the Knowledge Frontier F(K,P) separating established knowledge from unresolved requirements, telling Lord where to investigate next.

rows.anchor: Epistemic gap ... Gap(K,r) measures what is missing. EpistemicGap(K,P) = R(P)-SatisfiedRequirements(K). This is one of the most computationally useful concepts in Step 23. ... Gap closure ... a^* = \arg\max_a ExpectedGapReduction(a)/Cost(a). For high-risk decisions we can instead use Value of Inform
rows.statement: Defines EpistemicGap(K,P)=R(P)-SatisfiedRequirements(K), a highly useful concept, with two gap-closure prioritization rules (ExpectedGapReduction/Cost or VOI/Cost for high-risk decisions), connecting Steps 20-21.

rows.anchor: Minimum sufficient knowledge ... MSK(P) = Minimum Sufficient Knowledge for purpose P. We should not seek infinite knowledge. K\supseteq MSK(P) subject to the epistemic contract. This is important because otherwise KnowledgeOS could continue gathering information indefinitely.
rows.statement: Defines Minimum Sufficient Knowledge MSK(P): KnowledgeOS need only reach K⊇MSK(P), not gather unbounded information.

rows.anchor: Knowledge acquisition stopping rule ... Lord should stop investigating when Ready(K,P)=True or when VOI(a)<Cost(a) for remaining information actions, depending on policy. MoreInformation\neq AlwaysBetter. ... Diminishing information value ... VOI_1>VOI_2>VOI_3. At some point VOI_i\leq Cost_i. Then f
rows.statement: Establishes a principled stopping mechanism (Ready=True or VOI<Cost) — MoreInformation ≠ AlwaysBetter — while allowing Governance to override purely economic stopping rules for safety-critical/regulated actions.

rows.anchor: Epistemic debt ... EpistemicDebt meaning: Known deficiencies in the knowledge required for reliable operation or decision-making. Production migration: Epistemic debt = 3 unresolved critical requirements. This is analogous to technical debt, but concerns knowledge. ... Epistemic debt is measurable .
rows.statement: Introduces EpistemicDebt ED(P)=Σw_i·Gap_i as a technical-debt analogue for knowledge deficiency, warning a single critical gap must not be hidden inside an aggregate debt score.

rows.anchor: Knowledge quality dashboard ... KnowledgeHealth with coverage; freshness; unresolved conflicts; critical unknowns; evidence quality; provenance completeness; readiness; epistemic debt. This becomes an operational capability.
rows.statement: Proposes a KnowledgeHealth dashboard aggregating eight operational indicators (coverage, freshness, conflicts, critical unknowns, evidence quality, provenance completeness, readiness, epistemic debt).

rows.anchor: DDD: Epistemic Contract as a domain object ... Purpose, KnowledgeRequirements, EvidenceRequirements, AuthorityRequirements, FreshnessRequirements, UncertaintyTolerance, ConflictPolicy, Criticality, ReadinessPolicy. This belongs to the Epistemic/Knowledge Governance domain, not to the LLM layer. ...
rows.statement: Details the full EpistemicContract domain object (nine fields) belonging to the Epistemic/Knowledge Governance domain (not the LLM layer), and a KnowledgeRequirement object (eight fields) making readiness computable.

rows.anchor: Requirement dependency ... R_3=RollbackVerified may depend on R_2=BackupAvailable. R_2\rightarrow R_3. We therefore have a requirement dependency graph. ... Readiness propagation ... If R_2=Unknown, then R_3 may become Unknown. This can be calculated through dependency semantics. ... Circular requir
rows.statement: Defines a requirement dependency graph (e.g. Rollback depends on Backup) propagating Unknown status, warning the graph must be cycle-controlled to prevent non-terminating readiness computation.

rows.anchor: Computability ... Known(A), Supported(A), Sat(K,R), Coverage(K,P), CriticalGaps(K,P), Ready(K,P), Impact(K,A), VOI(a) when a valid decision model exists. So this is not merely philosophical.
rows.statement: Lists eight computationally realizable operations (Known, Supported, Sat, Coverage, CriticalGaps, Ready, Impact, VOI), establishing the sufficiency theory is not merely philosophical.

rows.anchor: But there is an important limit ... We cannot mathematically guarantee that K contains everything that exists in reality. There is no finite general-purpose test for Complete(K,Reality). Instead we can establish Sufficient(K,P) relative to an explicit purpose and contract. This is a crucial epistemo
rows.statement: States there is no finite general-purpose test for Complete(K,Reality) — only Sufficient(K,P) relative to an explicit contract is computable, reframing 'complete knowledge' claims into the auditable 'satisfied the epistemic contract for purpose P'.

rows.anchor: The KnowledgeOS answer contract ... AnswerStatus \{Established,Supported,Probable,Conditional,Incomplete,Disputed,Unknown,NotDetermined\}. And ReadinessStatus \{InformationReady,DecisionReady,ExecutionReady,NotReady\}. These should not be conflated. ... Example ... Current version: established ... R
rows.statement: Defines an eight-value AnswerStatus and four-value ReadinessStatus vocabulary, worked with a full migration-answer example far more informative than a bare yes/no.

rows.anchor: This gives Zero, Lord and Sārathi a very clean contract ... Zero FindGap(K,P) ... Lord FindActionsToCloseGap(Gap) ... Sārathi EvaluateWhetherGapMustBeClosed and DetermineDecisionReadiness. This is now an elegant division of responsibility.
rows.statement: Consolidates a clean three-way division: Zero=FindGap, Lord=FindActionsToCloseGap, Sārathi=EvaluateWhetherGapMustBeClosed+DetermineDecisionReadiness.

rows.anchor: Step 23 mathematical core ... R(P)=\{r_1,\ldots,r_n\} ... Sat(K,r_i) ... Coverage(K,P) ... CG(K,P)=\{r_i:Critical(r_i)\land\neg Satisfied(r_i)\} ... Ready(K,P) ... Gap(K,P)=R(P)\setminus Satisfied(K) ... VOI(a) ... K\supseteq MSK(P) subject to the epistemic contract.
rows.statement: Consolidates the full Step 23 mathematical core: requirements, satisfaction, coverage, critical gap set, readiness predicate, epistemic gap, VOI, and minimum sufficient knowledge.

rows.anchor:
Step 23 invariants ... S1 Sufficiency is purpose dependent ... S2 Completeness
eq Sufficiency ... S3 Knowledge volume
eq Knowledge sufficiency ... S4 High confidence in one assertion does not imply decision readiness ... S5 Unknown requirement
eq satisfied requirement ... S6 Critical knowledge ga
rows.statement: States sixteen candidate invariants S1-S16 covering purpose-dependent sufficiency, completeness/sufficiency/volume separations, unknown≠satisfied, uncollapsible critical gaps, epistemic-contract-gated readiness, information acquisition as action, non-monotonic information value, MSK preference, reality/knowledge state separation and lag, historical reconstructability, legitimate NotReady, and no universal completeness test.

rows.anchor: Step 23 verdict ... THEORETICALLY RESOLVED AT THE DOMAIN LEVEL ... We can compute sufficiency relative to an explicit epistemic contract. We cannot compute an absolute Complete(K,Reality) for arbitrary real-world knowledge. And we do not need to. That is actually an important theoretical result.
rows.statement: Declares Step 23 theoretically resolved at the domain level: sufficiency is computable relative to an explicit contract, absolute completeness of reality is not computable and is not needed — an important theoretical result.

rows.anchor: A major consequence for KnowledgeOS ... KnowledgeOS does not need to know everything. It needs to know whether it knows enough for the purpose at hand. KnowledgeOS Goal\neq \max |K| but KnowledgeOS Goal = \max\{Utility(K,P)\} subject to EpistemicContract(P). This prevents the architecture from becom
rows.statement: States the headline consequence: KnowledgeOS Goal ≠ max|K| but = max{Utility(K,P)} subject to EpistemicContract(P) — 'KnowledgeOS does not need to know everything, it needs to know whether it knows enough', preventing an infinite knowledge-collection machine.

rows.anchor: Our architecture is now becoming self-aware epistemically ... What it knows. Why it knows it. How certain that knowledge is. What it does not know. What is required to know more. Whether its current knowledge is sufficient for a specific action. That is a major architectural capability.
rows.statement: Lists six epistemic self-representation capabilities the architecture now provides (what it knows/why/how certain/what it doesn't know/what's needed/whether it's sufficient), calling this epistemic self-awareness architecturally (not consciousness) — a major capability.

rows.anchor: The emerging complete loop ... Reality \rightarrow Observation \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow Assertion \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow Knowledge ... Knowledge+Purpose \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment \rightarrow Ready/Gap ... Gap \rightarrow Zero \rightarrow Lord \rightarrow InformationAction \
rows.statement: Assembles the complete epistemic-operational control loop, branching on Ready vs Gap into two paths (Gap→Zero→Lord→InformationAction; Ready→Sārathi→Decision→Governance→Action→Outcome).

rows.anchor: Where I would take the theory next ... I would not immediately jump to implementation. We have accumulated enough formal pieces that we should next test whether they compose consistently. Step 24 — Formal Composition, Consistency, Invariants, and Closure of the KnowledgeOS Mathematical Model ... Can
rows.statement: Explicitly proposes Step 24 (Formal Composition, Consistency, Invariants, and Closure) testing sixteen consistency/computability properties across the whole Steps 1-23 model before declaring it closed — this is the exact step this batch processed as S0880, confirming the batch's numeric-order deviation.

lexical.anchor: When is the knowledge we have sufficient for the purpose for which we want to use it? The answer cannot be: When the LLM is confident. Nor: When we have enough documents. Nor: When the probability is above 95%. Sufficiency is always relative to a purpose.

conceptual.anchor: Zero's new role ... Zero can compare Requirements(P) against Knowledge(K). Then generate EpistemicDiscrepancy such as: Rollback capability is not established. This is different from an ordinary domain discrepancy. ... Lord's new role ... What action would close this epistemic gap? a_1=VerifyRollback

formal.anchor: Readiness as a predicate ... Ready(K,P) = HardSatisfied \land CriticalUncertaintyAcceptable \land ConflictAcceptable \land TemporalValid \land AuthoritySatisfied. This is much more robust.

governance.anchor:
Step 23 invariants ... S1 Sufficiency is purpose dependent ... S2 Completeness
eq Sufficiency ... S3 Knowledge volume
eq Knowledge sufficiency ... S4 High confidence in one assertion does not imply decision readiness ... S5 Unknown requirement
eq satisfied requirement ... S6 Critical knowledge ga

rationale_evidence.anchor: Readiness ... Ready(K,P) = the knowledge state contains sufficient validated information to perform the purpose P under the applicable rules and constraints. Ready(K,P) = \bigwedge_{r_i\in R_{hard}(P)} Satisfied(K,r_i) plus NoCriticalConflict and ApplicableGovernance. ... Readiness is not confidence
rationale_evidence.statement: Defines Ready(K,P) as a conjunction over all hard requirements plus no-critical-conflict and applicable-governance conditions, stating HighConfidenceInOneAssertion ≠ DecisionReadiness — one strongly-confirmed fact does not make the whole knowledge state ready.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Readiness is purpose-dependent ... For P_1=Inventory one trusted observation may be sufficient. For P_2=MigrationAuthorization we may require independent confirmation; current timestamp; system-of-record evidence. EvidenceRequirement(A,P_1)\neq EvidenceRequirement(A,P_2).
rationale_evidence.statement: Shows the same assertion's required evidence strength differs by purpose (inventory query vs migration authorization) — EvidenceRequirement(A,P1)≠EvidenceRequirement(A,P2).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge lag ... S_t\neq K_t. There may be a lag: ObservationLatency between RealityChange and KnowledgeUpdate. ... Staleness ... Freshness(A,t_2) must be evaluated. This connects Step 23 directly to Step 16. ... Temporal sufficiency ... A backup was verified six months ago. might be sufficient for
rationale_evidence.statement: Defines ObservationLatency between reality change and knowledge update, requiring Freshness(A,t) evaluation and a TemporalRequirement(P) in the Epistemic Contract — the same evidence can be sufficient for historical documentation but not for an imminent migration.

sources.note: A methodological pivot proposing that KR-ZERO-ORDER-2026-09's higher-order-Zero result be treated as mechanism-discovery evidence rather than a universal law, freezing as established: exists S such that individual Zero-status of every x in S does not imply Zero(S;D); Zero(x)&Zero(y) does not imply Zero({x,y}); and interaction order k is not globally monotone in |S|. Proposes a provisional research definition of interaction order ord_{T,Pi}(S;D)=min{k: Zero(S;D) is decidable from admissible information of order <=k}, and recommends resequencing the research programme as ORDER -> MECHANISM -> CARRIER -> REPRESENTATION-REDUCTION (rather than ORDER -> REPRESENTATION-REDUCTION directly), because the mathematical carrier (multiset/graph/hypergraph/rewrite-state) should be discovered from the elimination mechanism rather than assumed. Proposes a new experiment KR-ZERO-MECHANISM-2026-09 with three gates (denominator/accounting reconciliation across the historical 1395/1496/1475/1500 populations; complete witness extraction for the 115 irreducible cases; mechanism classification + minimal structural-dependency analysis per witness) before deciding the eventual carrier.

rows.anchor: ord_{T,Pi}(S;D) = min{k: Zero(S;D) is decidable from admissible information of order <= k}.
rows.statement: Defines a provisional (explicitly research, not ratified) interaction-order function ord_{T,Pi}(S;D) as the minimal information order at which Zero(S;D) becomes decidable, proposing to test whether order 1/2/3 correspond respectively to independent/local eliminability, pairwise interaction, and genuine three-way interaction, or whether that interpretation is false.

rows.anchor: N_generated = N_eligible + N_excluded + N_vacuous + N_invalid + ... 1500 != 1395 != 1496 != 1475 cannot simply be left implicit.
rows.statement: Demands a case-accounting identity reconciling every observed KR-ZERO population denominator (1500, 1395, 1496, 1475) before treating any percentage (89.7%, 8.24%, 90.04%, 7.89%) as a headline empirical estimate, framing this as an experimental-validity issue rather than documentation housekeeping.

rows.anchor: ORDER -> MECHANISM -> CARRIER -> REPRESENTATION REDUCTION ... KR-ZERO-MECHANISM-2026-09 ... let the mechanism experiment constrain the choice.
rows.statement: Recommends resequencing the research programme as ORDER -> MECHANISM -> CARRIER -> REPRESENTATION REDUCTION (rather than jumping straight to representation reduction), proposing a new experiment KR-ZERO-MECHANISM-2026-09 with three gates (denominator reconciliation; complete witness extraction for the 115 irreducible cases with a per-witness mechanism/minimal-dependency table; mechanism classification), so the eventual mathematical carrier (multiset, graph, hypergraph, rewrite system) is discovered from the elimination mechanism rather than promoted in advance.

rows.anchor: Zero_{T_n,Pi}(S_n;R^n) => Adeq(R^{n-1},Q,Pi) as the Zero-boundary hypothesis. I would not formulate it that strongly anymore ... Zero is itself a judgment produced by (D,T,Pi,S).
rows.statement: Rejects a proposed strong 'Zero-boundary hypothesis' (Zero at a reduction step implies adequacy of the next representation) as formulated too strongly, arguing instead that Zero is one observable judgment produced by the underlying tuple (D,T,Pi,S), with an unnamed interaction structure I_{T,Pi}(D,S) as the real open mathematical object -- reframing the research question from 'what does Zero predict?' to 'what structure determines the boundary at which reduction ceases to preserve the contract, of which Zero is one detection mechanism?'

rows.anchor: KR-ZERO discovered empirical constraints on context-dependent eliminability and revealed that relational structure may enter through the transformation/preservation pair. KR-REP-REDUCTION now independently investigates representation reduction ... using the KR-ZERO findings as controlled experimental factors and hypotheses -- not as definitions or conclusions.
rows.statement: Revises the relationship between the two experiment families: rather than 'KR-ZERO discovers eliminability; KR-REP-REDUCTION tests whether Zero predicts adequacy,' the corrected position is that KR-ZERO's findings become controlled experimental factors and hypotheses for KR-REP-REDUCTION, never definitions or conclusions it inherits; elevates the representation carrier (individual element vs subset vs relational structure/hypergraph/rewriting state) to a first-class unresolved research question that must be settled before R5->R2 can be properly designed.

rows.anchor: The eliminability of an information unit cannot, in general, be determined from the eliminability of its parts alone. ~89.7% ... ~2% ... ~0.2% ... ~8.2% ... irreducible ... explicitly refuses to promote this into a universal algebra.
rows.statement: Reframes the KR-ZERO-ORDER-2026-09 experiment's headline finding from 'Zero is higher-order' to the more precise claim that the eliminability of an information unit cannot in general be determined from the eliminability of its parts alone, giving the measured boundary: ~89.7% of tested levels singleton-determined, ~2% required pair information, ~0.2% required triple information, ~8.2% irreducible under the experiment's definition, with higher-order behavior strongly transformation-dependent, the effect surviving the provenance/contract audit, and an explicit refusal to promote the finding into a universal algebra.

rows.anchor: H-C was identified as structurally inapplicable to the specified deterministic sequential chain. ... a priori mathematical constraint != empirical falsification.
rows.statement: Endorses as a significant improvement in the project's epistemic discipline the correction distinguishing a priori mathematical constraint from empirical falsification, as applied to hypothesis H-C in the corrected KR-ZERO-ORDER writeup.

rows.anchor: Zero research: Can the eliminability of S be determined from information about its proper subsets? versus Representation reduction: How far can a representation be reduced while preserving Q under Pi? They are related, but they are not the same problem.
rows.statement: Endorses correctly separating 'Zero research' (can the eliminability of a set S be determined from information about its proper subsets) from 'representation reduction' (how far can a representation be reduced while preserving Q under Pi) as two related but distinct research objects, preventing the mistaken inference that finding Zero-phenomena is equivalent to having solved lossless knowledge extraction.

rows.anchor: D = [a,a,b,b] ... a1 -> Zero, a2 -> Zero, b1 -> Zero, b2 -> Zero, but {a1,a2} -> NOT Zero ... The effect of removing a group cannot necessarily be calculated by adding up the effects of removing its members individually ... a constraint on the future algebra, not evidence for a particular algebra ..
rows.statement: Highlights the irreducible example D=[a,a,b,b] where every individual element removal is Zero yet the pair removal {a1,a2} is not Zero, demonstrating that the effect of removing a group cannot necessarily be calculated by summing the effects of removing its members individually; insists this be treated as a constraint on a future algebra rather than evidence for any particular one, and approves the restraint of not yet committing to a specific mathematical structure (hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, tensor algebra).

rows.anchor: 'The carrier cannot be a set with an element-wise eliminability predicate.' ... A representation of eliminability based solely on independently assigned proper-subset Zero-status cannot, in general, determine group Zero-status ... What has been ruled out is set + independent element-wise eliminabili
rows.statement: Requests narrowing the claim 'the carrier cannot be a set with an element-wise eliminability predicate' to the safer statement that a representation of eliminability based solely on independently assigned proper-subset Zero-status cannot, in general, determine group Zero-status, since a future carrier could still be a set enriched with relations, context, transformation, and contract; what is ruled out is specifically 'set + independent element-wise eliminability' as a complete representation, not the use of a set carrier per se.

rows.anchor: Type 2 -- Contextual Zero and 8% irreducible are not necessarily the same phenomenon. Dimension A -- Context dependence: Zero(x|D1) != Zero(x|D2). Dimension B -- Determination order: Zero(S) cannot be derived from Zero-status of proper subsets. They may be related ... but the experiment hasn't demon
rows.statement: Corrects the proposed three-type Zero taxonomy by insisting that context-dependence (Dimension A: Zero(x|D1) != Zero(x|D2)) and determination-order failure (Dimension B: Zero(S) cannot be derived from proper-subset Zero-status) not be conflated as the same phenomenon merely because 'Type 2 -- Contextual Zero' and the '8% irreducible' result co-occur; they may be related or share a mechanism, but the experiment has not demonstrated they are identical.

rows.anchor: 'Zero is strictly an equivalence relation relative to an inquiry Q and preservation contract Pi' should not become part of the final theory unless we prove the equivalence-relation properties. Zero is currently a predicate / eliminability relation, not automatically an equivalence relation.
rows.statement: Rejects prematurely labeling Zero 'strictly an equivalence relation relative to inquiry Q and preservation contract Pi' unless reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity are actually proven under a precisely defined domain; until then Zero should be described only as a predicate/eliminability relation.

rows.anchor: Any future Knowledge Algebra must be capable of representing interaction between information units; independent unary importance values are insufficient for exact eliminability in the general case. ... Information -> value, provenance, context, relation, transformation, preservation contract -> inte
rows.statement: Derives an explicit architectural requirement from the KR-ZERO-ORDER result: any future Knowledge Algebra must be capable of representing interaction between information units, since independent unary importance values are insufficient for exact eliminability in the general case, sketching a pipeline from Information (value, provenance, context, relation, transformation, preservation contract) through an interaction structure to eliminability, while noting the mathematical structure of that interaction remains one of the most interesting open questions.

rows.anchor: Information cannot always be classified as removable by evaluating each piece independently. Therefore a future knowledge-extraction system cannot safely rely only on token importance, entity importance, frequency, salience scores, or independent 'relevance' classifications if it wants exact contrac
rows.statement: Frames a business-facing consequence of the Zero-order result: because information cannot always be classified as removable by evaluating each piece independently, a future knowledge-extraction system cannot safely rely only on token importance, entity importance, frequency, salience scores, or independent relevance classifications if it wants exact contract-level preservation, and must instead be capable of reasoning about groups and relationships.

rows.anchor: We're getting closer to knowing what the algebra must be able to express. That's different from knowing what the algebra is. Transform / Preserve / Eliminate -> Interaction -> Boundary -> ??? mathematical structure. The ??? is still the research problem.
rows.statement: States plainly that the project has NOT yet solved Knowledge Algebra: it is getting closer to knowing what the algebra must be able to express (support Transform, Preserve, Eliminate operations, feeding into an Interaction structure and a Boundary) but the actual mathematical structure realizing that interaction remains an open research problem, explicitly marked '???' in the current architecture sketch.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS research has demonstrated that information eliminability is contract- and transformation-dependent, and that exact elimination cannot in general be determined from independent properties of individual information units. This establishes a concrete constraint for the future Knowledge Alge
rows.statement: Offers a one-sentence business summary of the whole Zero research phase -- information eliminability is contract- and transformation-dependent and exact elimination cannot in general be determined from independent unit properties, establishing a concrete constraint that any future Knowledge Algebra must represent structural interaction rather than merely independent information relevance -- and characterizes the epistemic progress as moving from 'maybe there is an algebra' to 'if an algebra exists for this problem, we now have experimentally established properties it must satisfy', explicitly short of 'we solved Knowledge Algebra'.

rows.anchor: I would freeze this result as evidence before adding anything from the palmistry/Nadi book. The latter can now be used to generate candidate hypotheses about what kinds of relational structures might matter, without contaminating the independent evidence base.
rows.statement: Decides to freeze the corrected KR-ZERO-ORDER result as evidence before incorporating anything from the palmistry/Nadi book reading, restricting the book strictly to generating candidate hypotheses about what kinds of relational structures might matter, so as not to contaminate the independent evidence base.

rows.anchor: k=1: 1,252/1,395=89.7%; k=2: 25/1,395=1.8%; k=3: 3/1,395=0.2%; irreducible: 115/1,395=8.2%. Zero is usually singleton-determined, but a substantial minority of tested levels requires relational information beyond singleton status, and some levels cannot be determined from any proper-subset Zero-stat
rows.statement: Confirms the corrected KR-ZERO-ORDER ladder (k=1 89.7%, k=2 1.8%, k=3 0.2%, irreducible 8.2%) survives correction and reframes the headline claim from 'Zero is higher-order' to the more precise statement that Zero is usually singleton-determined, a substantial minority of tested levels requires relational information beyond singleton status, and some levels cannot be determined from any proper-subset Zero-status at all.

rows.anchor: T2 dedup: 28.2%; T8 interacting: 22.9%; T4 context: 11.2%; everything else <=0.8%; T7: 0%. Transformation choice materially affects interaction-order behavior. ... the later mechanism experiment had already produced element-wise counterexamples, so the stronger universal claim really must remain wit
rows.statement: Endorses narrowing the transformation claim from 'relational transformations produce higher-order behavior, element-wise ones do not' to the transformation-specific per-transformation interaction rates (T2 dedup 28.2%, T8 interacting 22.9%, T4 context 11.2%, others <=0.8%, T7 0%), to be frozen only as 'transformation choice materially affects interaction-order behavior', noting the later mechanism experiment already produced element-wise counterexamples that force withdrawal of the stronger universal claim.

rows.anchor: All contracts: size tests 1,475, k=1 1,327, k=2 25, k=3 6, Irreducible 117/7.93%. Excluding cancelling: size tests 1,496, k=1 1,337, k=2 17, k=3 15, Irreducible 127/8.49%. The phenomenon survives removal of the problematic contract and, if anything, the higher-order strata become more visible.
rows.statement: Reports the paired/provenance robustness correction comparing 'all contracts' (1475 size tests, k1=1327, k2=25, k3=6, irreducible 117=7.93%) against 'excluding cancelling' (1496 size tests, k1=1337, k2=17, k3=15, irreducible 127=8.49%), finding the higher-order-Zero phenomenon survives removal of the problematic cancelling contract and the higher-order strata become more visible, yielding a genuine robustness-supported empirical finding rather than an artifact of one parameterization.

rows.anchor: requiring order 2 at size 3 does not imply requiring >=2 at size 4 ... k is a local property of the particular elimination level, rather than a globally accumulating 'complexity budget.'
rows.statement: Endorses the properly-scoped negative result that requiring interaction order 2 at subset size 3 does not imply requiring order >=2 at size 4, preventing the unjustified model k(m+1)>=k(m); the experiment instead indicates that determination order k is a local property of the particular elimination level, not a globally accumulating complexity budget.

rows.anchor: D=[a,a,b,b] with deduplication ... All four singleton removals are Zero, but Zero({0,1})=false while Zero({0,2})=true. Thus two groups can have exactly the same singleton-level description but different group-level eliminability ... a very clean counterexample to any model of the form Zero(S)=f(Zero
rows.statement: Highlights the irreducibility witness D=[a,a,b,b] under deduplication where all four singleton removals are individually Zero, yet Zero({0,1})=false while Zero({0,2})=true, so two groups with identical singleton-level descriptions have different group-level eliminability, giving a clean counterexample to any model of the form Zero(S)=f(Zero(x1),...,Zero(xn)), constraining any representation storing only independent proper-subset Zero-status.

rows.anchor: withdraws 'the carrier cannot be a set with an element-wise eliminability predicate' and replaces it with ... 'set + independent element-wise eliminability is insufficient as the complete representation.' You have not ruled out Set + relations + context + T + Pi. You have only ruled out independent
rows.statement: Endorses narrowing the carrier conclusion from 'the carrier cannot be a set with an element-wise eliminability predicate' to 'set + independent element-wise eliminability is insufficient as the complete representation', clarifying that a carrier of Set + relations + context + transformation + contract remains entirely possible; only independent unary Zero-status has been ruled out as a complete description of group eliminability, an important constraint but not yet a carrier selection.

rows.anchor: I would not freeze this sentence: 'Type 2 is the centre.' ... change to: 'Context dependence is a central observed dimension of the broader Zero problem, but its causal relationship to higher-order determination remains OPEN.'
rows.statement: Rejects freezing the interpretive sentence 'Type 2 is the centre' (the three Zero 'types' being descriptive vocabulary rather than established categories), replacing it with 'context dependence is a central observed dimension of the broader Zero problem, but its causal relationship to higher-order determination remains OPEN', preserving the insight while declining to convert it into a finding.

rows.anchor: 'Three independent occurrences now' for FR-001, KR-ZERO-GROUP G5, and KR-ZERO-ORDER. I'd use: 'Three distinct constructions exhibit the same obstruction shape.' ... local/pairwise information -> insufficient -> higher-order structure appears in three different research constructions. That is a resea
rows.statement: Requests replacing 'three independent occurrences' (referring to FR-001, KR-ZERO-GROUP G5, and KR-ZERO-ORDER) with 'three distinct constructions exhibit the same obstruction shape', since 'independent' wrongly implies unestablished statistical/experimental independence, and classifies the pattern of local/pairwise information being insufficient to imply higher-order structure appearing across three constructions as a research hypothesis generator, not yet a theorem.

rows.anchor: KR-ZERO asks: Can S be eliminated without changing the relevant result? KR-REP-REDUCTION asks: How far can D be transformed while preserving Q under Pi? ... The current evidence does not justify Zero===Preservation, and KR-REP-REDUCTION has actually provided evidence against using Zero as a simple p
rows.statement: Argues that because KR-ZERO (can S be eliminated without changing the relevant result) and KR-REP-REDUCTION (how far can D be transformed while preserving Q under Pi) study eliminability and representation-preservation respectively, and because KR-REP-REDUCTION has provided evidence against using Zero as a simple preservation-boundary criterion, keeping the two research programs analytically separate is now even more strongly justified.

rows.anchor: Singleton determination dominates tested cases (~90%) [EXP] ... Set carrier is ruled out [NOT ESTABLISHED / withdrawn] ... Three Zero 'types' are established laws [NOT ESTABLISHED] ... Zero defines preservation boundary [NOT SUPPORTED] ... General Knowledge Algebra [OPEN].
rows.statement: Issues a final 14-row canonical KR-ZERO epistemic ledger, tagging each finding [EXP]/[NEG/EXP]/[NOT ESTABLISHED]/[OPEN/PROP]/[NOT SUPPORTED], explicitly retiring 'set carrier is ruled out' to [NOT ESTABLISHED/withdrawn] and 'three Zero types are established laws' and 'local->higher-order obstruction is universal' to [NOT ESTABLISHED], while keeping singleton-domination, higher-order-determination-exists, triple-requiring cases, ~8% irreducibility, transformation-affects-order, context-dependence, and unary-insufficiency all at [EXP].

rows.anchor: KR-ZERO = empirical constraint system, rather than KR-ZERO = completed algebra. And the strongest result to carry forward ... Independent local eliminability information is insufficient, in general, to determine group eliminability.
rows.statement: States the bottom line that KR-ZERO has reached the scientific maturity of an empirical constraint system rather than a completed algebra, with the single strongest result to carry forward being that independent local eliminability information is insufficient, in general, to determine group eliminability -- a genuine constraint any future KnowledgeOS reduction/elimination formalism must satisfy.

rows.anchor: I would freeze this corrected KR-ZERO result separately from the pending KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09. ... Do not yet merge the two evidence bases into Theory v1.3. The corrected KR-ZERO result is now strong enough to be preserved as evidence, while the representation-reduction experiment still ne
rows.statement: Decides to freeze the corrected KR-ZERO result as historical evidence separately from the pending KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09, explicitly declining to merge the two evidence bases into Theory v1.3 until the representation-reduction experiment completes its forensic audit.

rows.anchor: 'Proves higher-order interaction exists for n<=6' -> change 'proves' to 'demonstrates empirically within the tested generator/design for n<=6.' ... [EXP] higher-order determination occurs in the tested system, not a mathematical proof of a general phenomenon.
rows.statement: Corrects the phrase 'proves higher-order interaction exists for n<=6' to 'demonstrates empirically within the tested generator/design for n<=6', since k>3 remains open and n<=6 is only a design bound, tagging the result [EXP] higher-order determination occurs in the tested system rather than a mathematical proof of a general phenomenon.

rows.anchor: 'Element-wise transformations yield k=1 or 0%' should not appear in the canonical classification ... from our earlier mechanism experiment we already know this was subsequently falsified: there were element-wise irreducible witnesses under P9_balance. The canonical formulation should be: 'Transforma
rows.statement: Retracts the canonical claim 'element-wise transformations yield k=1 or 0%' since the mechanism-order experiment already produced element-wise irreducible witnesses under transformation P9_balance falsifying it, replacing it with the canonical formulation that transformation choice materially affects the observed determination-order distribution and relational transformations are strong generators in this corpus but relationality is neither necessary nor sufficient for higher-order Zero.

rows.anchor: 21x23 decomposes into right vertical, crosswise, left vertical interaction ... X otimes Y = L(X,Y) + I(X,Y) + R(X,Y) where L=local/invariant contribution, I=interaction/cross contribution, R=remainder/carry. ... A combined result can contain interaction terms that do not exist in either component in
rows.statement: Extracts a local-plus-interaction decomposition from Vertically-and-Crosswise multiplication, proposing X otimes Y = L(X,Y)+I(X,Y)+R(X,Y) (local, interaction, and remainder/carry contributions), analogous to the empirical finding that group behavior can differ from independent member behavior in the Zero research.

rows.anchor: F(x,y)=F_x(x)+F_y(y)+F_xy(x,y). The cross term is not reducible to the independent contributions. That maps remarkably well onto our ORDER findings. We already found that some group-level Zero status cannot be determined from the Zero statuses of proper subsets.
rows.statement: Reconfirms the interaction-algebra reading of Vertically-and-Crosswise multiplication (F(x,y)=F_x(x)+F_y(y)+F_xy(x,y), with an irreducible cross term), noting it maps onto the ORDER research finding that group-level Zero status cannot always be determined from proper-subset Zero statuses.

rows.anchor: C(x,y) != C(x)+C(y). There may be an interaction term I(x,y). Contr(x,y)=Contr(x)+Contr(y)+I(x,y). Then it becomes perfectly possible that Zero(x)=Zero(y)=1 while Zero(x,y)=0. The interaction term can reintroduce observable contribution. This is exactly the sort of thing we should test, not declare
rows.statement: Proposes a candidate mathematical explanation for the prior finding that group-level Zero cannot be recovered from individual Zero statuses: a contribution decomposition Contr(x,y)=Contr(x)+Contr(y)+I(x,y) with an interaction term I(x,y) that can reintroduce observable contribution even when Zero(x)=Zero(y)=1, so Zero(x,y)=0 is possible -- explicitly marked as something to test, not declare as a law.

rows.anchor: Zero-A: contribution Zero, C(x)=0, the item contributes neither positively nor negatively. Zero-B: observational Zero, Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_x(D))), the item can be removed without changing the observation. These are not automatically equivalent. It is possible that C(x)=0 but removing x changes some othe
rows.statement: Distinguishes contribution-Zero (Zero-A: C(x)=0, neither positive nor negative contribution) from observational-Zero (Zero-B: the standard Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_x(D))) removability condition), arguing they are not automatically equivalent -- a zero-contribution item might still be observationally non-removable, and conversely two nonzero, cancelling contributions (C(x1)+C(x2)=0) could produce group-level neutrality without either being individually Zero, echoing the earlier ORDER findings.

rows.anchor: Zero != Cancellation. Suppose C(a)=+1 and C(b)=-1. Then C(a)+C(b)=0. But Zero(a)!=true and Zero(b)!=true. The pair is neutral. This could explain why group-level behavior can differ from individual Zero status. It gives us a candidate algebraic mechanism for the higher-order phenomena we observed. A
rows.statement: Formalizes Zero != Cancellation via the example C(a)=+1, C(b)=-1 summing to zero (the pair is neutral) while neither a nor b is individually Zero, proposed as a candidate algebraic mechanism explaining why group-level behavior can differ from individual Zero status, explicitly marked hypothesis, not conclusion.

sources.note: Step 223 (phase_measure_theory): freezes the historical falsification audit protocol -- a 9-field per-step record R_i=(C,E,K,D,I,M,V,G,X), claim/evidence/status taxonomies, concept naming triad, decision tuple, invariant-vs-principle distinction, formula provenance protocol, Gita extraction+temporal test, contradiction/evolution handling, three architecture states (intended/implemented/verified), two-pass History->Data->Architecture discipline, concept metrics (Freq, W(k), OriginCount, Convergence, Divergence), genealogy graph, four-layer H->C->F->A evidence model with Gita as parallel G<->C layer, AI-candidate acceptance pipeline, and status vocabulary AI_Candidate->...->Architecture_Verified.

rows.anchor: No more architecture synthesis during extraction.
rows.statement: Step 223 changes the mode of operation: extraction must stop synthesizing architecture; the boxed rule is 'No more architecture synthesis during extraction' -- we must first reconstruct what Steps 1-182 actually contain before any architectural claim.

rows.anchor: R_i=(C_i,E_i,K_i,D_i,I_i,M_i,V_i,G_i,X_i)
rows.statement: For every step S_i (1<=i<=182) the audit constructs a 9-field record R_i=(claims C_i, evidence E_i, concepts K_i, decisions D_i, invariants I_i, formal models M_i, verification V_i, Gita relationship G_i, contradictions/unresolved issues X_i).

rows.anchor: Step 37 explicitly claims X, based on evidence Y, and derives interpretation Z.
rows.statement: Extraction must not summarize a step coarsely ('Step 37 discusses provenance'); it must state claim+evidence+interpretation precisely, and must preserve the distinction between SourceStatement (what the historical text says) and AuditorInterpretation (the auditor's reading of it).

rows.anchor: Type(C)\in\{Existence,Behavior,Causality,Intent,Interpretation,Normative,Philosophical\}
rows.statement: Claim extraction: every substantive claim gets an identifier C_{i,j} (step i, claim number j, e.g. C_{37,4}) and a Type drawn from the closed set {Existence, Behavior, Causality, Intent, Interpretation, Normative, Philosophical}.

rows.anchor: E\in\{Implementation,Experiment,Observation,Document,Decision,Discussion,AIAnalysis,Retrospective\}
rows.statement: Evidence extraction: for every claim C_{i,j}, its evidence E(C_{i,j}) is classified into {Implementation, Experiment, Observation, Document, Decision, Discussion, AIAnalysis, Retrospective}; this immediately exposes claims with no primary support.

rows.anchor: Direct | Corroborated | Supported | Inferred | Speculative | Contradicted | Unknown
rows.statement: Evidence status vocabulary (to remain stable through the audit): Direct (explicitly demonstrated), Corroborated (supported independently by multiple sources), Supported (limited evidence), Inferred (reasonable interpretation), Speculative (possible but insufficiently supported), Contradicted (evidence points against it), Unknown (insufficient evidence).

rows.anchor: Only later may we determine whether this belongs to Identity\neq State.
rows.statement: Concept extraction K_i={k_1,...,k_n} must not immediately map a concept to the candidate architecture (e.g. record 'ImmutableIdentifier' as a raw concept, not yet as belonging to Identity!=State) -- this prevents confirmation bias.

rows.anchor: Source term | Normalized | Candidate architectural interpretation
rows.statement: Independent concept naming safeguard: maintain three columns per concept -- Source term (exactly what the historical material calls it), Normalized term (controlled vocabulary for cross-step analysis), Candidate architectural interpretation (current, explicitly provisional interpretation); worked example maps 'trace'->Traceability->Provenance, 'history'->Historical record->Temporal lineage, 'approval'->Authorization->Governed action.

rows.anchor: D=(Problem,Options,Decision,Rationale,Authority,Evidence,Time)
rows.statement: Decision extraction: every decision D_{i,j} is captured as the 7-tuple (Problem, Options, Decision, Rationale, Authority, Evidence, Time); missing fields must be recorded as Unknown rather than inferred from later knowledge.

rows.anchor: Problem\rightarrow Options\rightarrow Decision\rightarrow Architecture\rightarrow Implementation
rows.statement: A decision should be traceable along the chain Problem->Options->Decision->Architecture->Implementation; any missing link in this genealogy must remain visibly marked '?' rather than silently filled in.

rows.anchor: Principle\neq Invariant
rows.statement: An invariant is stronger than a principle/statement: 'the system should preserve provenance' is a principle, while the implication EveryGeneratedArtifact => HasProvenance is an invariant candidate; Principle != Invariant must be kept distinct during extraction.

rows.anchor: 1. formula; 2. variables; 3. assumptions; 4. derivation; 5. interpretation; 6. source; 7. engineering application; 8. verification status.
rows.statement: Mathematical extraction protocol: every formula M_{i,j} must be recorded independently with 8 fields -- formula, variables, assumptions, derivation, interpretation, source, engineering application, verification status -- flagged as especially important given the corpus's later introduction of distribution theory, inference, uncertainty and model validation.

rows.anchor: must not simply appear in the final book as "the architecture's formula."
rows.statement: Formula provenance requirement: e.g. the empirical CDF estimator hat F_n(x) must not be claimed as 'the architecture's formula' without establishing WHY it was introduced -- an actual model of system behavior, an analogy, a statistical experiment, a theoretical framework, or a later synthesis are completely different claims and must not be conflated.

rows.anchor: chapter; verse/reference if available; original technical context; philosophical interpretation; whether the Gita was present at that time; whether the relationship is P1, P2 or P3.
rows.statement: Gita extraction schema G_{i,j} per Chapter 1-4 reference: chapter, verse/reference, original technical context, philosophical interpretation, whether the Gita was actually present at that historical time, and the P1/P2/P3 relationship classification; GitaReference != ArchitecturalEvidence.

rows.anchor: TechnicalConcept\rightarrow GitaReflection ... then the relationship is likely P3
rows.statement: Gita temporal test: if the technical concept existed before the Gita interpretation was introduced (TechnicalConcept -> GitaReflection), the relationship is likely P3 unless evidence establishes earlier influence; if the Gita was explicitly used to generate the engineering concept (Gita -> TechnicalConcept), P1 may be justified.

rows.anchor: contradiction; involved claims; contexts; time; possible explanation; unresolved/resolved status.
rows.statement: Contradiction extraction: for each step's contradiction set X_i={x_1,x_2,...}, record the contradiction, involved claims, contexts, time, possible explanation, and resolved/unresolved status; contradictions must not be hidden.

rows.anchor: Contradiction\neq Error ... HistoricalRevision from LogicalInconsistency
rows.statement: A later statement legitimately contradicting an earlier one may represent architectural Evolution rather than Error; the audit must distinguish HistoricalRevision from LogicalInconsistency, i.e. Contradiction != Error automatically.

rows.anchor: A_1\rightarrow A_2\rightarrow A_3\rightarrow A_4. Not: A=A_4
rows.statement: A mature architecture must be represented as an evolution chain A_1->A_2->A_3->A_4, never as though the final state A_4 had always existed -- flagged as especially important for reconstructing KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: A^{intended} ... A^{implemented} ... A^{verified}. Thus: A=(A^{intended},A^{implemented},A^{verified})
rows.statement: Three architecture states per concept: A=(A^intended, A^implemented, A^verified). Possible state (True,False,False) is an 'architectural gap'; (True,True,False) is an 'assurance gap'.
invariants: A = (A^intended, A^implemented, A^verified) as a triple of independently-valued booleans/statuses

rows.anchor: Pass 1: History->Data. Pass 2: Data->Architecture. Never reverse the order.
rows.statement: Candidate-family mapping to Family_A..Family_H must happen only after extraction, via a mandatory two-pass discipline: Pass 1 History->Data, Pass 2 Data->Architecture; the order must never be reversed.

rows.anchor: must equally search for EvidenceAgainstSemanticIntegrity ... This is the falsification requirement.
rows.statement: Preventing confirmation bias during Pass 1: the auditor must search equally for evidence AGAINST each candidate principle (EvidenceAgainstSemanticIntegrity, EvidenceAgainstIdentity!=State, EvidenceAgainstKnowledge!=Authority) as for supporting evidence -- the falsification requirement.

rows.anchor: | Step | Claim | Evidence | Concept | Decision | Invariant | Formula | Gita | Contradiction | Status |
rows.statement: The final extraction table (one row per step, 1-182, columns Claim/Evidence/Concept/Decision/Invariant/Formula/Gita/Contradiction/Status) becomes the 'historical evidence dataset' underlying all subsequent synthesis.

rows.anchor: Importance(k)\neq Freq(k) ... W(k)=\sum_i w(E_i,k) ... Direct>Corroborated>Supported>Inferred>Speculative
rows.statement: Concept frequency Freq(k)=|{S_i: k in S_i}| is insufficient on its own (Importance(k) != Freq(k): a concept mentioned 50 times by AI analysis is not necessarily stronger than one directly demonstrated once in implementation); a better measure is evidence-weighted recurrence W(k)=sum_i w(E_i,k) using the qualitative ordering Direct>Corroborated>Supported>Inferred>Speculative, aimed at comparison rather than fake numerical precision.

rows.anchor: OriginCount(k) ... Convergence(k)=|IndependentOrigins(k)| ... HighConvergence\not\Rightarrow Truth ... Divergence(k)=|\text{distinct meanings of }k|
rows.statement: Independent origin count OriginCount(k) counts genuinely independent discovery paths (e.g. Experiment, DDD, Governance arriving separately at the same concept is more significant than repetition within one conversation); Convergence(k)=|IndependentOrigins(k)| but HighConvergence does NOT imply Truth, only that multiple reasoning paths converged. Divergence(k)=|distinct meanings of k|; if Divergence(Evidence)>1, 'Evidence' may not be one domain concept but several bounded-context concepts.

rows.anchor: This is where DDD becomes empirically testable ... BoundedContext becomes a stronger hypothesis.
rows.statement: Divergence analysis makes DDD empirically testable: instead of declaring bounded contexts from intuition, identify SemanticClusters where a concept (e.g. Evidence_Engineering vs Evidence_Governance) repeatedly clusters around different meanings, then test whether the clusters share identity/lifecycle/invariants/ownership/language -- if not, BoundedContext becomes a stronger hypothesis.

rows.anchor: G_C=(C,E) ... Introduces, Refines, Specializes, Contradicts, Combines, Implements, Verifies.
rows.statement: The genealogy graph G_C=(C,E) has concepts as nodes and edges typed {Introduces, Refines, Specializes, Contradicts, Combines, Implements, Verifies}, intended to show the evolution of thought; only from this graph is ConceptGraph->InvariantGraph->ArchitectureGraph derived -- architecture is reconstructed from the graph, not imposed from above.

rows.anchor: H\rightarrow C\rightarrow F\rightarrow A ... A\rightarrow Evidence\rightarrow H'.
rows.statement: The four-layer evidence model: Layer 1 Historical (H, what actually happened), Layer 2 Conceptual (C, what concepts emerged), Layer 3 Formal (F, mathematical/logical structures), Layer 4 Architectural (A, resulting software architecture); boxed as H->C->F->A with a feedback loop A->Evidence->H', called a much stronger reconstruction model than simply writing an architecture document.

rows.anchor: GitaReflection is a parallel interpretive layer: G\leftrightarrow C rather than G\rightarrow A.
rows.statement: The Gita must not be forced into the H->C->F->A chain; instead it sits as a parallel interpretive layer G<->C (can illuminate concepts C) rather than G->A (directly producing architecture) -- this preserves intellectual honesty.

rows.anchor: AIAnalysis\rightarrow CandidateInterpretation. It is not automatically AIAnalysis\rightarrow Fact.
rows.statement: AI analysis (DeepSeek/Claude/ChatGPT) must be modeled as AIAnalysis->CandidateInterpretation, never automatically AIAnalysis->Fact; AI outputs become architectural knowledge only via Evidence->Human/EngineeringAssessment->Acceptance -- directly relevant to whether DeepSeek's suggestions could be accepted.

rows.anchor: Candidate\rightarrow EvidenceCheck\rightarrow ContradictionCheck\rightarrow HistoricalCheck\rightarrow TechnicalCheck\rightarrow ArchitecturalAcceptance.
rows.statement: The acceptance pipeline for an AI-derived candidate principle: Candidate->EvidenceCheck->ContradictionCheck->HistoricalCheck->TechnicalCheck->ArchitecturalAcceptance, yielding an AcceptedPrinciple only at the end.

rows.anchor: AI\_Candidate ... Evidence\_Supported ... Engineering\_Validated ... Architecture\_Accepted ... Architecture\_Implemented ... Architecture\_Verified.
rows.statement: Proposed status vocabulary for AI-derived architecture forming a governance chain: AI_Candidate -> Evidence_Supported -> Engineering_Validated -> Architecture_Accepted -> Architecture_Implemented -> Architecture_Verified.

rows.anchor: What we observed ... What we inferred ... What we formalized ... What we built ... What we verified ... What we later understood philosophically.
rows.statement: The book can distinguish six epistemic layers of claim ('what we observed' / 'inferred' / 'formalized' / 'built' / 'verified' / 'later understood philosophically'); this distinction is proposed as potentially one of the strongest methodological contributions of the work.

rows.anchor: Extract first. Interpret second.
rows.statement: Step 223 verdict: the extraction protocol is frozen conceptually as 'Extract first. Interpret second.' The audit must preserve History+Evidence+Concepts+Decisions+Invariants+Mathematics+GitaReflection+Contradictions before legitimately answering what architecture actually emerged from Steps 1-182.

rationale_evidence.statement: Formula provenance requirement: e.g. the empirical CDF estimator hat F_n(x) must not be claimed as 'the architecture's formula' without establishing WHY it was introduced -- an actual model of system behavior, an analogy, a statistical experiment, a theoretical framework, or a later synthesis are completely different claims and must not be conflated.

rationale_evidence.statement: Divergence analysis makes DDD empirically testable: instead of declaring bounded contexts from intuition, identify SemanticClusters where a concept (e.g. Evidence_Engineering vs Evidence_Governance) repeatedly clusters around different meanings, then test whether the clusters share identity/lifecycle/invariants/ownership/language -- if not, BoundedContext becomes a stronger hypothesis.
