sources.note: A frozen external research lens (2026-09-06) treating observable reciprocal biological interaction sequences (e.g. courtship signal/response chains) as a source of structural hypotheses for KnowledgeOS, with a formal observation-unit/interaction-trace model, a four-layer anti-leakage translation architecture (Biological Observation->Abstract Structure->Software Analogue->KnowledgeOS Evaluation), six frozen research questions (R1-R6) on element/sequence/contract-relative Zero, hypothesis dynamics, decision stability and historical divergence, and explicit anti-anthropomorphism/anti-leakage rules. Structurally analogous to the corpus's Vedic/philosophical external lenses but grounded in biology; no prior object matches.

rows.anchor: EXT-BIOCOMM-2026-09 ... Status: [EXT][RESEARCH LENS] — FROZEN
rows.statement: A finalized external research-lens specification (Biological Reciprocal Communication Lens) investigating observable reciprocal interaction sequences in biological systems as a source of structural hypotheses for KnowledgeOS, explicitly NOT treating biology as an implementation of KnowledgeOS; Theory v1.2 frozen, kernel untouched, no Knowledge Algebra axioms added.

rows.anchor: Observation ≠ Interpretation and Interpretation ≠ Determination.
rows.statement: An observed behaviour (e.g. animal A approaching animal B) does not by itself license an interpretive conclusion (e.g. 'A wants X'); any interpretation enters the research pipeline only as an explicitly identified hypothesis.

The fundamental observation unit (actor, observable signal, observable response, temporal position, observable context) forms an ordered, order-sensitive interaction trace, examined at four structural levels: Element, Relation, Sequence, and Contextual interaction (explicitly a research decomposition, not a KnowledgeOS kernel-level claim).

rows.anchor: B → A(B) → S(A) → KOS(S)
rows.statement: A four-layer 'defensive translation architecture' (biological observation -> abstract directed-graph structure -> multi-agent software analogue -> KnowledgeOS evaluation) is required before any KnowledgeOS construct (state transformation, preservation, eliminability, hypothesis transitions, determination, decision stability, historical divergence) may be applied, to prevent biological terminology from silently becoming KnowledgeOS ontology.

rows.anchor: Zero_{T,Π}(S;D) ⟺ Π(T(D)) = Π(T(E_S(D))) ... an apparently insignificant event can become indispensable when the preservation contract changes.
rows.statement: Zero is explicitly not assigned biologically (ignored != Zero, rejected != non-Zero); it is evaluated only after the transformation and preservation contract (Pi_1 immediate state, Pi_2 terminal outcome, Pi_3 targeted historical provenance, which must not silently become 'preserve everything') are specified.

rows.anchor: R1 — Non-Elementarity ... R6 — Historical Divergence
rows.statement: Six frozen research questions with explicit witness conditions and explicit non-overclaim caveats: whether element-level Zero determines sequence-level Zero (R1), order sensitivity of Zero under segment exchange (R2), contract-relative Zero for the same element (R3), hypothesis-space dynamics after a response (R4, sign of change not predetermined), decision stability despite unresolved causal hypothesis (R5, explicitly not to be read as biological rationality/intentionality), and whether different interaction histories can converge on the same terminal state (R6, testing TerminalStateEquivalence not implying HistoricalEquivalence).

rows.anchor: The following substitutions are prohibited unless independently justified: Signal⇒Intent, Silence⇒Rejection, Approach⇒Desire, Withdrawal⇒Refusal, Response⇒Acceptance, Behaviour⇒Knowledge.
rows.statement: An explicit anti-anthropomorphism rule and a companion anti-leakage rule (no biological observation may directly become a KnowledgeOS axiom; [EXT]->[PROP] does not imply [PROP]->[CORE]) bound the lens as behavioural-structural rather than a theory of animal mental states.

rows.anchor: Do not immediately create another theory document. ... Lens Freeze → Pre-registration → O-F* → Synthetic Witness Generator → Controls → Execution → Adjudication
rows.statement: Recommends KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 as the next artifact — a pre-registration plus synthetic witness generator running the R1-R6 tests on controlled synthetic traces first, biological examples serving only as structural inspiration, explicitly citing the O-F* protocol as part of the required execution order.

rows.anchor: e_i=(S_i,M_i,R_i,t_i,C_i) ... observable signal != semantic message ... response != epistemic acceptance.
rows.statement: Defines the primitive biological interaction event e_i=(S_i,M_i,R_i,t_i,C_i) (sender, observable signal/behavior, observable receiver response, temporal position, context) and an ordered interaction episode C^{t:n}=[e_1,...,e_n], with the explicit boundary that observable signal != semantic message and response != epistemic acceptance until later interpretation layers assign meaning.

rows.anchor: B -> A(B) -> S(A) -> KOS(S) ... This prevents animal behavior -> KnowledgeOS primitive from happening implicitly.
rows.statement: Specifies a four-layer interpretation pipeline B (biological observation) -> A(B) (abstract structure, e.g. G=(V,E)) -> S(A) (software analogue trace) -> KOS(S) (KnowledgeOS evaluation of Zero, H, Determination, Decision, State Transition), explicitly to prevent animal-behavior-to-KnowledgeOS-primitive inference from happening implicitly.

rows.anchor: absence of observed response != knowledge of rejection ... response classification != epistemic classification.
rows.statement: Argues non-response (R_B=empty_observed following A's signal M) must not be inferred as 'B ignored M'; the hypothesis space instead includes not-perceived, perceived-but-no-response, response-outside-observation-channel, environmental-constraint, competing-behavior, etc., giving 'absence of observed response != knowledge of rejection' and, symmetrically for opposing responses, 'response classification != epistemic classification.'

rows.anchor: R1 Non-elementarity ... R2 Order sensitivity ... R3 Contract relativity ... R4 Hypothesis-space transformation ... R5 Decision stability ... R6 History divergence
rows.statement: Reduces the lens's prior five research questions to six (R1 non-elementarity, R2 order sensitivity, R3 contract relativity, R4 hypothesis-space transformation measuring both |H_{t+1}|-|H_t| and the transition relation R without assuming direction, R5 decision stability, R6 history divergence K1~=K2 while Hist1 not-equiv_{Pi_prov} Hist2), and specifies what the lens MAY generate (candidate operators/distinctions/algebraic properties, counterexamples, DDD vocabulary) versus MAY NOT establish (axioms, kernel membership, truth conditions, universal animal intentions, mathematical laws via metaphor).

rows.anchor: Knowledge Graph != Knowledge State != Knowledge Algebra. ... I would replace the old name "Courtship Signalling Lens" with Biological Reciprocal Communication Lens
rows.statement: Separates Knowledge Graph (representation of the interaction) from Knowledge State from Knowledge Algebra (what can legitimately be concluded from the graph), and renames the lens from 'Courtship Signalling Lens' to 'Biological Reciprocal Communication Lens', treating courtship as its first experimental domain rather than its definition.

lineage_claims.quote: I would replace the old name "Courtship Signalling Lens" with: Biological Reciprocal Communication Lens

rows.anchor: Yes. I would rewrite it as a Biological Communication Research Lens, rather than a "courtship metaphor."
rows.statement: This file duplicates S2826's 'Biological Communication Research Lens' content verbatim, and duplicates it again within itself; it contributes no content beyond what S2826 already records (observation event e_i, B->A(B)->S(A)->KOS(S) pipeline, non-response boundary, R1-R6, renaming to Biological Reciprocal Communication Lens).

lineage_claims.quote: identical text to S2826, and to itself repeated within this file

rows.anchor: e_i = (A_i, sigma_i, O_i, t_i, C_i) ... Hypothesis formulation H occurs only inside the explicit interpretation layer (Interpretation(sigma_i, O_i, C_i) -> H)
rows.statement: De-biologizes the observation unit from e_i=(S_i,M_i,R_i,t_i,C_i) to e_i=(A_i,sigma_i,O_i,t_i,C_i) (observed actor, observable signal, observable response, time, context), explicitly isolating observables and requiring hypothesis formulation H to occur only inside an explicit interpretation layer Interpretation(sigma_i,O_i,C_i)->H, to protect KnowledgeOS primitives from assumed intentions.

lineage_claims.quote: De-biologized Observation Unit

rows.anchor: R1 (Non-Elementarity) ... R2 (Order Sensitivity vs. Non-Commutativity) ... R3 (Contract Relativity) ... R4 (Hypothesis Dynamics) ... R5 (Action Stability) ... R6 (Historical Identity)
rows.statement: Presents refined R1-R6 witness criteria: R1 tests z(C1)=z(C2) and Zero(C1)!=Zero(C2); R2 formally bounds Zero(C1oC2)!=Zero(C2oC1) as an observational order witness, not intrinsic algebraic non-commutativity; R3 tests Pi2 (terminal) vs Pi3 (provenance-preserving) contracts to show Outcome Equivalence != Historical Equivalence; R4 bounds Delta|H| in {<0,=0,>0} without assuming a direction; R5 replaces 'epistemic closure' with policy invariance |H_Q|>1 and |pi(H_Q)|=1; R6 tests T(K0,C1)=T(K0,C2) with Hist(C1) not-equiv_{Pi3} Hist(C2).

rows.anchor: I would change the wording in R3 ... to: A positive witness establishes, within the tested domain, that eliminability varies with preservation contract. Likewise R6
rows.statement: Corrects R3's and R6's overclaiming wording ('proves that eliminability varies by preservation contract'; 'establishes that state equivalence does not imply historical identity') to witness-relative statements ('a positive witness establishes, within the tested domain/representation/provenance contract, that ...'), preserving the distinction between an experimental witness and a universal theorem.

rows.anchor: Element => Relation => Sequence => History ... information sufficient at one level may be insufficient at the next.
rows.statement: Proposes that Knowledge Algebra may have a structure where Element does not imply Relation does not imply Sequence does not imply History: Z1=[Zero(e1),Zero(e2),...] might not determine Z2=Zero(e1,e2), which might not determine Z3=Zero(C^{t:n}), which itself might not determine historical provenance; connects this directly to prior Zero-algebra results where group/sequence Zero could not reliably be inferred from singleton Zero, while noting the biological lens does not itself establish this, only provides an independent test domain.
missing: actual witness demonstrating the non-implication chain

rows.anchor: Biological Lens Principle: Biological reciprocal interaction is used as an external generator of observable relational, sequential, and historical structures. No biological interpretation is promoted into KnowledgeOS semantics unless it survives explicit abstraction, formalization, and independent capability testing.
rows.statement: Freezes the 'Biological Lens Principle': biological reciprocal interaction is used only as an external generator of observable relational/sequential/historical structures, and no biological interpretation is promoted into KnowledgeOS semantics unless it survives explicit abstraction, formalization, and independent capability testing; the research chain is Biological Observation -> Abstract Structure -> Software Realization -> KnowledgeOS Experiment -> Witness -> Independent Replication, never Biology -> KnowledgeOS Axiom directly.

rows.anchor: G_t = representational structure ... K_t = epistemic state ... Theta = state transformation ... with Zero evaluating preservation
rows.statement: Ties the biological interaction graph representation to existing architecture by distinguishing G_t (representational structure, what is connected) from K_t (epistemic state) from Theta (state transformation), with Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) evaluating preservation across them; the graph tells us what is connected, KnowledgeOS machinery determines what those connections mean epistemically.

rows.anchor: Freeze the lens ... Build the empirical corpus ... Create the biological -> abstract compiler ... Run R1 first: Non-elementarity ... the next artifact should be the R1 pre-registration + observation/translation schema, not another conceptual rewrite.
rows.statement: Lays out a concrete execution order: freeze the lens; build an empirical corpus of observable (not interpreted) reciprocal-interaction events; build a biological-to-abstract compiler preserving only explicitly declared structural properties; run R1 (non-elementarity) as the first actual experiment, then R2 (order), R3 (preservation-contract relativity), R4 (hypothesis-space transition), R5 (action stability), R6 (history vs state); proposes a directory structure (00-lens/01-corpus/02-translation/03-experiments/04-controls/05-witnesses) and states the next artifact should be the R1 pre-registration and translation schema, not another conceptual rewrite.

rows.anchor: Observation != Interpretation and Interpretation != Determination. ... those may become hypotheses only after an explicit interpretation layer.
rows.statement: States the frozen lens's epistemic boundary: an observed courtship behavior does not by itself establish intention, interpretation, acceptance, rejection, knowledge, consent, or causal understanding; Observation != Interpretation and Interpretation != Determination, and any interpretation enters the pipeline only as an explicitly identified hypothesis.

rows.anchor: Layer 1 -- Biological Observation ... Layer 2 -- Abstract Structure ... Layer 3 -- Software Analogue ... Layer 4 -- KnowledgeOS Evaluation ... This prevents biological terminology from silently becoming KnowledgeOS ontology.
rows.statement: Specifies the frozen four-layer defensive translation architecture (Biological Observation -> Abstract Structure G=(V,E) -> Software Analogue multi-agent trace -> KnowledgeOS Evaluation of state transformation/preservation/eliminability/hypothesis transitions/determination/decision stability/historical divergence), explicitly to prevent biological terminology from silently becoming KnowledgeOS ontology.

rows.anchor: Pi_1: Immediate State ... Pi_2: Terminal Outcome ... Pi_3: Targeted Historical Provenance ... Pi_3 must not silently become "preserve everything."
rows.statement: Defines three preservation-contract scopes for the lens: Pi1 (immediate state following an interaction), Pi2 (terminal outcome of the interaction episode), Pi3 (targeted historical provenance, e.g. {EventOrder,ActorIdentity,Timestamp,CausalLink}); Pi3 must not silently become 'preserve everything', and the purpose is to test whether OutcomeEquivalence != HistoricalEquivalence.

rows.anchor: Element elimination ... Relation elimination ... Subsequence elimination ... The exact implementation must be fixed before an experiment.
rows.statement: Defines three granularities of the elimination operator on an interaction trace C^{t:n}: element elimination E_{e_i}(C), relation elimination E_{(e_i,e_j)}(C), and subsequence elimination E_{C^{a:b}}(C), requiring the exact implementation to be fixed before any experiment.

rows.anchor: The following substitutions are prohibited unless independently justified: Signal=>Intent, Silence=>Rejection, Approach=>Desire, Withdrawal=>Refusal, Response=>Acceptance, Behaviour=>Knowledge.
rows.statement: States an explicit anti-anthropomorphism rule prohibiting six substitutions by default (Signal=>Intent, Silence=>Rejection, Approach=>Desire, Withdrawal=>Refusal, Response=>Acceptance, Behaviour=>Knowledge), making the lens a behavioural-structural lens rather than a theory of animal mental states.

rows.anchor: No biological observation can directly introduce a KnowledgeOS primitive. ... [EXT] -> [PROP] does not imply [PROP] -> [CORE].
rows.statement: States an explicit anti-leakage rule: the permitted direction is Biological Observation -> Structural Candidate -> Formal Specification -> Capability Test, never Biological Observation -> KnowledgeOS Axiom; and promotion from [EXT] to [PROP] does not imply promotion from [PROP] to [CORE].

rows.anchor: Convergence != Proof. Cross-lens agreement is evidence for further investigation, not automatic theoretical promotion.
rows.statement: States a cross-lens verification rule: results from the biological lens should be tested independently using other lenses (Information Theory, Bayesian Epistemology, Kalman/State Estimation, Non-Classical Logic, Knowledge Graphs, Cybernetics, Vedic/philosophical research), but the purpose is not to obtain automatic confirmations -- Convergence != Proof, cross-lens agreement is evidence for further investigation only.

rows.anchor: An interaction must be evaluated by what distinction it preserves or destroys under an explicitly specified contract, not by the biological meaning assigned to the interaction. ... Frozen Lens != Confirmed Findings.
rows.statement: States the lens's final research principle: an interaction must be evaluated by what distinction it preserves or destroys under an explicitly specified contract, not by the biological meaning assigned to it (Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) is evaluated from preserved observable structure, not semantic labels); and explicitly separates a Frozen Lens (how we investigate) from Confirmed Findings (what we will find) -- freezing the lens as a research methodology does not freeze any empirical proposition as true.

rows.anchor: Zero Algebra <-> Zoom/Resolution <-> Biological Reciprocal Communication ... none of the three gets to dictate the others.
rows.statement: Identifies a triangle of three mutually-informing but non-dictating research programmes: Zero Algebra (eliminability tests), Zoom/Resolution (resolution changes), and Biological Reciprocal Communication (relational sequences), all evaluated through Knowledge Theory's epistemic semantics and contracts, with none entitled to define the KnowledgeOS kernel.

rows.anchor: At coarse resolution C^(r)=[sigma_1,rho_1,sigma_2,rho_2] might be eliminable ... Zooming in ... can expose distinctions that were invisible at the coarse level. Therefore Zero^(r)(C)=1 does not imply Zero^(r+1)(C)=1
rows.statement: Applies the resolution-relative-eliminability idea to a concrete courtship-sequence example: at coarse resolution the sequence [sigma1,rho1,sigma2,rho2] might be eliminable with respect to a terminal-state inquiry, while a finer resolution exposing orientation/distance/timing/repeated-approach/avoidance can reveal distinctions invisible at the coarse level, giving both Zero^(r)(C)=1 does not imply Zero^(r+1)(C)=1 and its converse Zero^(r)(C)=0 does not imply Zero^(r+1)(C)=0.

rationale_evidence.statement: Argues non-response (R_B=empty_observed following A's signal M) must not be inferred as 'B ignored M'; the hypothesis space instead includes not-perceived, perceived-but-no-response, response-outside-observation-channel, environmental-constraint, competing-behavior, etc., giving 'absence of observed response != knowledge of rejection' and, symmetrically for opposing responses, 'response classification != epistemic classification.'

rationale_evidence.anchor: Zero Algebra <-> Zoom/Resolution <-> Biological Reciprocal Communication ... none of the three gets to dictate the others.
rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies a triangle of three mutually-informing but non-dictating research programmes: Zero Algebra (eliminability tests), Zoom/Resolution (resolution changes), and Biological Reciprocal Communication (relational sequences), all evaluated through Knowledge Theory's epistemic semantics and contracts, with none entitled to define the KnowledgeOS kernel.

sources.note: S0889's Step 25A.4: crosses conceptual->executable; eighteen numbered experiments walking K0 through K6 across acquisition/assessment/commitment/conflict/temporal-resolution/invalidation/dependency-propagation/replay/determinism/AI-hallucination/AI-extraction/anti-hindsight; discovers KnowledgeRevision=GraphImpactAnalysis+Reassessment with a first O(N+M) complexity estimate; consolidates I1-I10 invariants and a first kernel architecture diagram; verdicts PASS (viable) with four open areas, explicitly not claiming mathematical closure; hands off to Step 25A.5 (property-based falsification).

rows.anchor: We now cross the important boundary: Conceptual model \rightarrow Executable state machine. The purpose of 25A.4 is not to build production KnowledgeOS. It is to see whether our current mathematical model can actually execute a sequence of knowledge transitions without violating the invariants disco
rows.statement: Announces crossing from conceptual model to executable state machine, testing whether a sequence of knowledge transitions can execute without violating prior invariants.

rows.anchor: The experiment ... K_0 \xrightarrow{event_1} K_1 \xrightarrow{event_2} K_2 \cdots \xrightarrow{event_n} K_n. Every transition must be explicit; reproducible; traceable; temporally identifiable; reversible/replayable through history; unable to silently change historical states. The fundamental functi
rows.statement: Defines the fundamental transition function T(K_t,e_t)→K_{t+1} required to be explicit, reproducible, traceable, temporally identifiable, replayable, and unable to silently mutate history.

rows.anchor: Minimal state ... K_t = (A_t,E_t,Q_t,C_t,D_t,V_t) ... Assertions, Evidence, Assessments, Conflicts, Derivation/dependency relations, Temporal validity. And outside K_t: G for the current goal, and EC for the epistemic contract. This is intentionally small.
rows.statement: Defines the minimal six-field executable KnowledgeState K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Assessments,Conflicts,Derivations,TemporalValidity) with Goal and EpistemicContract kept external.

rows.anchor: Immutable snapshots ... K0 = empty, K1 = K0 + Evidence E1 + Assertion A1, K2 = K1 + Evidence E2 + Assertion A2, K3 = K2 + Conflict C1, K4 = K3 + Resolution R1, K5 = K4 + Retraction E1. We never execute K1.modify(...). Instead K1 → K2.
rows.statement: Defines a worked six-snapshot immutable state sequence (K0-K5), explicitly forbidding in-place mutation.

rows.anchor: Event model ... EvidenceRegistered, AssertionCreated, AssessmentRecorded, AssertionCommitted, ConflictDetected, ConflictResolved, EvidenceInvalidated, AssertionSuperseded, AssertionRetracted, DerivationCreated, SnapshotCreated. This is already revealing something important: KnowledgeState is natural
rows.statement: Defines an eleven-event vocabulary, observing that KnowledgeState is naturally event-evolvable (mathematically compatible with event sourcing) without committing to it as a production implementation choice.

rows.anchor: Experiment 1 — Empty state ... K_0=\varnothing. We calculate Hash(K_0)=h_0. The hash is not the mathematical state itself. It gives us a useful integrity mechanism for the experiment. ... Experiment 2 — Register evidence ... e_1=EvidenceRegistered(E_1). T(K_0,e_1)=K_1. E_1\in K_1. But A_1\notin K_1
rows.statement: Works Experiment 1 (empty state with an integrity hash) and Experiment 2 (evidence registration), confirming evidence entering K1 does not automatically create the corresponding assertion — registering evidence does not automatically create knowledge.

rows.anchor: Experiment 3 — Assessment ... q_1=Assess(E_1,A_1). relevance = high, directness = direct, temporal_fit = valid, authenticity = verified, dependency = independent, conflict = none. Then Q_1(A_1)=q_1. Still A_1 is not necessarily committed. ... Experiment 4 — Commitment ... e_3=Commit(A_1). Subject to
rows.statement: Works Experiment 3 (assessment with six concrete field values) and Experiment 4 (contract-gated commitment producing an explicit commitment boundary K3∋A1).

rows.anchor: Experiment 5 — Duplicate evidence ... E_1'=E_1. We require Register(E_1')=NoSemanticDuplicate. Register(Register(E))=Register(E) at least with respect to semantic state. This is an idempotency requirement.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 5 testing idempotent duplicate registration: Register(Register(E))=Register(E) with respect to semantic state.

rows.anchor: Experiment 6 — Independent corroboration ... E_2 from an independent direct observation. E_1\vdash A_1 and E_2\vdash A_1. The system should increase the evidential support for A_1, but must not simply count sources. We need Independence(E_1,E_2). This confirms the earlier statistical requirement.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 6 (independent corroboration) confirming that increasing evidential support requires an explicit Independence(E1,E2) check, not simple source counting.

rows.anchor: Experiment 7 — Contradiction ... E_3: Version(Nexus)=3.72.0. Create A_2. Now A_1\perp A_2 under the same context/time. Generate C_1=Conflict(A_1,A_2). The state becomes K_4=\{A_1,A_2,C_1\}. Both remain visible.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 7 (contradiction) producing K4={A1,A2,C1} with both assertions and the conflict marker retained.

rows.anchor: Experiment 8 — Temporal resolution ... A_1: Version=3.69 [t_0,t_1] ... A_2: Version=3.72 [t_2,\infty) where t_1<t_2. Re-evaluate Conflict(A_1,A_2). Result: False. This is an extremely important result. The conflict engine must operate on semantic scope, not simply values.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 8 showing disjoint validity intervals resolve the apparent conflict to False, called an extremely important result: the conflict engine must operate on semantic scope, not raw values.

rows.anchor: Experiment 9 — Evidence invalidation ... the inventory from which it came is discovered to have been faulty. e_9=Invalidate(E_1). K_5=T(K_4,e_9). But we do not delete E_1. Instead E1.status = Invalid and Dependents(E_1) are identified. ... Dependency propagation ... E_1\rightarrow A_1\rightarrow A_4
rows.statement: Works Experiment 9 (invalidation without deletion, E1.status=Invalid) followed by dependency propagation producing an Impact(E1) reassessment cascade through the derivation chain.

rows.anchor: Experiment 10 — Partial support survives ... Support(A_1)=\{E_1,E_2\}. Invalidate E_1. Then Support(A_1)=\{E_2\}. If E_2 is sufficient: Status(A_1)=Supported. If not: Status(A_1)=Uncertain. Retraction(E)\not\Rightarrow Retraction(A) automatically. This is a major invariant.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 10 showing partial support survival after one evidence item is invalidated, establishing the major invariant Retraction(E) ⇏ Retraction(A) automatically.

rows.anchor: Experiment 11 — Derived assertion ... A_1 and A_5. Rule: A_1\land A_5\Rightarrow A_6. Record D_1=(A_1,A_5\vdash A_6). Now invalidate A_1. We must automatically identify A_6 as affected.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 11 (derived assertion) requiring automatic identification of a downstream derived assertion (A6) as affected when a premise (A1) is invalidated.

rows.anchor: Experiment 12 — Knowledge can become unknown ... A_1.status=Committed. After invalidation of its only support: A_1.status=Unknown. Not False. Not Deleted. Known \rightarrow Unknown is a valid knowledge transition.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 12 (one of the most important tests) establishing Known→Unknown as a valid knowledge transition, distinct from becoming False or Deleted.

rows.anchor: Experiment 13 — Historical state ... K_3 contained A_1. Later K_6 does not accept A_1. We must still be able to query K_3\models A_1. HistoricalState(K_3) remains unchanged. This passes our historical immutability requirement.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 13 confirming a superseded historical snapshot remains queryable and unchanged, passing the historical immutability requirement.

rows.anchor: Experiment 14 — Replay ... Replay(K_0,e_1,\ldots,e_6)=K_6. This gives us Replayability. If replay produces a different state K_6'\neq K_6, we have discovered a serious defect. ... Experiment 15 — Determinism ... T(K,e)=T(K,e) on repeated execution. Register(E_1) should produce the same semantic stat
rows.statement: Works Experiment 14 (full replay reconstruction, framed as revealing a serious defect if the replayed state diverges) and Experiment 15 (determinism, T(K,e) reproducible on repeated execution).

rows.anchor: Experiment 16 — AI output ... L_1="Rollback has been successfully verified." with no supporting artifact. Support(A_{AI})=\varnothing. Therefore Commit(A_{AI})=False. The assertion remains Candidate/Unsupported. The state machine survives the hallucination.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 16 confirming the state machine correctly rejects commitment of an unsupported LLM hallucination, remaining Candidate/Unsupported.

rows.anchor: Experiment 17 — AI extraction ... Rollback test executed at 14:30. Restore completed successfully. AI extracts A_{AI2}: RollbackVerified=True. But provenance becomes A_{AI2} \rightarrow LLMExtraction \rightarrow Artifact \rightarrow Source. The LLM is recorded as a transformation, not as the ultimat
rows.statement: Works Experiment 17 (legitimate LLM extraction from a real report) confirming the correct provenance chain A→LLMExtraction→Artifact→Source is achieved — exactly the intended architecture.

rows.anchor: Experiment 18 — Historical decision ... K_{10} had Rollback=Unknown. A decision is made D_{10}=DoNotMigrate. At t_{11}, we learn Rollback=True. We must not alter D_{10}. Instead D_{10} remains the decision made under K_{10}. This passes the anti-hindsight invariant.
rows.statement: Works Experiment 18 confirming the anti-hindsight invariant passes: a historical decision remains unaltered even after later evidence would have changed it.

rows.anchor: What the executable model now demonstrates ... K_0 \rightarrow K_1 \rightarrow K_2 \rightarrow K_3 \rightarrow K_4 \rightarrow K_5 \rightarrow ... and transitions can represent acquisition; assessment; commitment; conflict; temporal resolution; invalidation; revision; derivation; historical reconstr
rows.statement: States this is the first serious indication the theory has an executable core: a coherent multi-step K0→K1→...→Kn transition sequence spanning nine kinds of operation.

rows.anchor: But we have also discovered a deeper issue ... Invalidate(E_1) can affect A_1,A_2,A_3,\ldots,D_1,D_2,\ldots,Decision. Therefore the computation potentially requires traversing a dependency graph. KnowledgeRevision = GraphImpactAnalysis + Reassessment. This will matter enormously for scalability.
rows.statement: Discovers KnowledgeRevision = GraphImpactAnalysis + Reassessment: invalidating one evidence item can require traversing a whole dependency graph, an important scalability concern.

rows.anchor: First computational complexity question ... N=|KnowledgeGraph| and invalidating one evidence item requires traversing all downstream dependents, worst-case propagation may approach O(N+M) where M is the number of dependency edges. This is manageable for many graphs, but not automatically trivial at
rows.statement: Gives the first computational complexity estimate: worst-case O(N+M) for dependency-graph invalidation propagation, judged manageable but not automatically trivial at scale, deliberately deferring optimization until correctness is established.

rows.anchor: The state-machine invariants ... I1 Historical immutability K_t never changes after creation. I2 Explicit revision K_t\rightarrow K_{t+1} requires an event/cause. I3 Provenance Every committed assertion has traceable support. I4 No silent contradiction Conflicts remain represented. I5 Temporal valid
rows.statement: Consolidates ten candidate state-machine invariants I1-I10 (historical immutability, explicit revision, provenance, no silent contradiction, temporal validity, unknown preservation, dependency propagation, AI boundary, replayability, idempotency) directly derived from the eighteen experiments.

rows.anchor: The first genuine architectural boundary ... KnowledgeOS Kernel ... Input → Evidence → Assessment → Assertion → KnowledgeState → Revision/Conflict → Provenance/Temporal. Everything else can build on this. This is much more defensible than starting with an "AI agent" abstraction.
rows.statement: Sketches the first genuine kernel architectural boundary diagram (Evidence→Assessment→Assertion→KnowledgeState→Revision/Conflict→Provenance/Temporal), argued more defensible than starting from an AI-agent abstraction.

rows.anchor: 25A.4 Verdict ... PASS — Minimal executable state model is viable but with four significant open mathematical areas: 1. Evidence aggregation. 2. Conflict resolution. 3. Revision/impact propagation. 4. Statistical assessment. The important distinction is that these are no longer vague philosophical q
rows.statement: Verdicts Step 25A.4 PASS — the minimal executable state model is viable, with four remaining open mathematical areas now recast as explicit computational interfaces rather than vague philosophical questions, called major progress.

rows.anchor: What we should NOT conclude ... We should not yet conclude: "KnowledgeOS mathematics is solved." We have shown something narrower: A coherent executable epistemic state machine can be constructed from the current theory. That is a much stronger result than merely having conceptual definitions, but i
rows.statement: Explicitly refuses to conclude 'KnowledgeOS mathematics is solved', narrowing the actual result to: a coherent executable epistemic state machine can be constructed from the current theory — stronger than conceptual definitions alone, but not mathematical closure.

rows.anchor: Next step: 25A.5 ... Step 25A.5 — Property-Based Falsification of the Knowledge State. Here we stop constructing happy-path examples. Instead we generate hundreds/thousands of randomized state transitions containing conflicting evidence; duplicate evidence; stale evidence; invalid evidence; AI-gener
rows.statement: Proposes Step 25A.5: property-based falsification via randomized generation of state-transition sequences across thirteen adversarial categories, automatically testing invariants I1-I10 for counterexamples — a counterexample being more valuable than another successful happy-path example.

rows.statement: Summarizes the 25A.1-25A.5 progression as types→evidence→revision→executable-state→falsification, framing it as scientifically meaningful groundwork before proceeding to Zero and discrepancy computation.

sources.note: Step 201's canonical, single-meaning-per-term vocabulary freeze for the whole KnowledgeOS architecture: sixteen frozen terms each with a canonical question and formal role, invariants I_70 (identity stability) and I_73 (no implicit semantic elevation), and the resulting 'not a data model, a semantic transition architecture' framing.

rows.anchor: One concept must have one semantic identity. And conversely: One word must not silently represent multiple concepts.
rows.statement: States the central rule of the vocabulary freeze: one concept must have exactly one semantic identity, and one word must never silently stand for multiple concepts -- a DDD and mathematical integrity operation, not mere terminology cleanup.

rows.anchor: \mathcal K = (I,S,O,E,P,A,M,U,R,D,X,L) with: Transition, Process, Invariant as structural mechanisms operating over these concepts.
rows.statement: Assembles the candidate canonical vocabulary as a twelve-symbol tuple (Identity, State, Observation, Evidence, Proposition, Assessment, Model, Uncertainty, Authority, Decision, Action, Lineage) plus Transition/Process/Invariant as structural mechanisms operating over them -- the basis to be challenged term by term.

rows.anchor: I_{70}: A state transition must not silently change the identity of the subject.
rows.statement: Canonical definition of Identity ('which thing are we talking about?'): identity remains stable across state changes (x_t=x_{t+1} while State(x_t)!=State(x_{t+1})); grounds invariant I_70 that a state transition must never silently change the subject's identity.

rows.anchor: CurrentState\neq History. History is a sequence: H_x=(S_0,S_1,\ldots,S_n).
rows.statement: Canonical definition of State ('what is the condition of the domain object at time t?'): explicitly not the same as History, which is the full sequence of states.

rows.anchor: O=(subject,time,observer,content). ... Observation \not\Rightarrow Truth.
rows.statement: Canonical definition of Observation ('what was observed?') as the tuple (subject,time,observer,content); an observation is an event of perception/measurement that does not automatically constitute truth.

rows.anchor: Evidence may originate from: observation; document; measurement; system event; human testimony; validated AI output; derived computation. But evidence requires provenance.
rows.statement: Canonical definition of Evidence ('what information is being used to support or challenge a proposition?'), naming seven possible origins and requiring provenance; connects via supports/contradicts edges to Proposition.

rows.anchor: Proposition \neq Assessment. The proposition is the claim. The assessment is our current evaluation of that claim.
rows.statement: Canonical definitions of Proposition (the claim itself, e.g. 'Deployment D completed successfully') and Assessment (Assessment=f(Proposition,Evidence,Model,Uncertainty), the current evaluation of the claim, drawn from {Supported,Refuted,Unknown,Ambiguous,Conflicted}) as two distinct concepts that must never be conflated.

rows.anchor: M=(Assumptions,Rules,Parameters). ... model identity/version belongs in lineage.
rows.statement: Canonical definition of Model ('under what interpretation or formal assumptions are we evaluating the evidence?') as (Assumptions,Rules,Parameters), with model identity/version required to be tracked in lineage since different models can legitimately produce different assessments from the same evidence.

rows.anchor: U=UncertaintyStructure rather than necessarily: U\in[0,1]. ... numerical; interval-based; categorical; structural; semantic; causal; temporal.
rows.statement: Canonical definition of Uncertainty ('what remains unresolved, imprecise, probabilistic, ambiguous, or model-dependent?') as a general UncertaintyStructure rather than necessarily a scalar in [0,1], with seven possible forms (numerical, interval, categorical, structural, semantic, causal, temporal).

rows.anchor: Authority(a,x,c,t). ... Authority is therefore: Contextual+Temporal+Scoped.
rows.statement: Canonical definition of Authority ('who or what is legitimately empowered to perform or approve an action in this context?') as Authority(actor,action,context,time) -- contextual, temporal, and scoped.

rows.anchor: TechnicalPermission\neq DomainAuthority. This should become a permanent vocabulary rule.
rows.statement: Explicitly separates Permission from Authority as a permanent vocabulary rule: a technical UPDATE-database permission does not mean authorization to approve a business decision.

rows.anchor: Decision\neq Truth. ... Decision\neq Action. ... Decision=ApproveDeployment but: Action=DeploymentExecuted. The decision may exist even if execution never happens.
rows.statement: Canonical definitions of Decision ('what choice was made?', not implying correctness) and Action ('what was actually done?', distinct from Decision), illustrated by an approved-but-unexecuted deployment.

rows.anchor: Outcome=f(Action,Environment). ... Outcome is not necessarily controlled by the actor.
rows.statement: Canonical definition of Outcome ('what happened as a consequence of an action?') as a function of Action and Environment, fundamentally different from intention and not necessarily controlled by the acting party.

rows.anchor: a transition is not synonymous with 'state changed.' ... Process\neq Transition. ... an invariant must always have an explicit scope. ... I_domain may not automatically be: I_global.
rows.statement: Canonical definitions of Transition (a formal state-or-process-recording mechanism, not synonymous with 'state changed'), Process (a composed sequence of transitions with ordering/dependencies/conditions/orchestration/completion semantics, distinct from a single Transition), and Invariant (a condition that must remain true within an explicit scope, since a domain-level invariant is not automatically global).

rows.anchor: L(x) = {origin,parents,transformations,times,actors}. ... Lineage\neq Truth.
rows.statement: Canonical definition of Lineage ('where did this thing come from, what contributed to it, and through which transformations did it pass?') as {origin, parents, transformations, times, actors}, supporting auditability/reproducibility/explanation/reconstruction/dependency-analysis, but explicitly not itself Truth.

rows.anchor: Observation -> Evidence -> Proposition -> Assessment -> Decision -> Action -> Outcome while: Authority constrains: Decision/Action, and: Model+Uncertainty constrain: Assessment. And: Lineage cross-cuts the entire chain.
rows.statement: Consolidates the complete semantic chain of the frozen vocabulary: the core Observation->Evidence->Proposition->Assessment->Decision->Action->Outcome chain, with Authority constraining Decision/Action, Model+Uncertainty constraining Assessment, and Lineage cross-cutting the whole chain -- 'the architecture is no longer a collection of nouns, it has a semantic flow'.

rows.anchor: Knowledge_t -> Decision_t -> Action_t -> Observation_{t+1} -> Knowledge_{t+1}. The architecture therefore supports continuous learning without assuming that every new observation invalidates everything previously known.
rows.statement: States the KnowledgeOS learning loop Knowledge_t->Decision_t->Action_t->Observation_{t+1}->Knowledge_{t+1}, supporting continuous learning without assuming every new observation invalidates all prior knowledge.

rows.anchor: Loss of actor memory \neq loss of system lineage. ... Epistemic continuity can be preserved even when actor memory is not.
rows.statement: Formalizes the Chapter-4 lens once more: an actor's incomplete knowledge (K_a(t) subset K_system(t)) does not mean the system's historical lineage L(K_a(t)) is lost -- epistemic continuity can be preserved even when actor memory is not, proposed as a major book concept.

rows.anchor: We should not encode 'Krishna' as a literal architectural component. The useful abstraction is: Perspective is not the same as total system knowledge.
rows.statement: Explicitly warns against literalizing the Krishna metaphor as an architectural component; the safe abstraction is LocalActorPerspective subset GlobalHistoricalPerspective -- perspective is not the same as total system knowledge.

rows.anchor: 'The AI knows...' unless we specify what that means. ... 'The current state contains the history...' unless historical lineage is actually preserved.
rows.statement: Names six specific vocabulary patterns as architectural smells to be rejected: 'the AI knows', 'the system is confident', 'the user has permission' (meaning authority), 'the decision is correct' (meaning authorized), 'the evidence proves' (meaning supports), and 'the current state contains the history' (unless lineage is actually preserved).

rows.anchor: Frozen: Identity, State, ... Lineage. Introduced and provisionally accepted: KnowledgeArtifact, SemanticElevation. These two need further testing.
rows.statement: Formally classifies sixteen terms as Frozen (Identity, State, Observation, Evidence, Proposition, Assessment, Model, Uncertainty, Authority, Decision, Action, Outcome, Transition, Process, Invariant, Lineage) and two terms (KnowledgeArtifact, SemanticElevation) as provisionally accepted pending further testing.

rows.anchor: We should not create one giant: KnowledgeObject containing: identity state evidence decision authority action uncertainty ... That would destroy bounded-context integrity.
rows.statement: Draws the most important DDD consequence of the vocabulary freeze: never create one giant KnowledgeObject aggregating identity/state/evidence/decision/authority/action/uncertainty, since that destroys bounded-context integrity; e.g. EvidenceAggregate should not automatically own DecisionAggregate -- the relationship should instead be Decision-basedOn->EvidenceReference, keeping ownership and lifecycle separate.

rows.anchor: Identity/Domain, Observation/Evidence, EpistemicAssessment, Governance/Authority, Decision/Action, Lineage with: Process as an orchestration mechanism across them. This is not yet the final bounded-context map.
rows.statement: Proposes a first, explicitly provisional six-part structural decomposition (Identity/Domain, Observation/Evidence, EpistemicAssessment, Governance/Authority, Decision/Action, Lineage) with Process as a cross-cutting orchestration mechanism -- the vocabulary-derived candidate, not yet the final bounded-context map.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not primarily a data model. It is a semantic transition architecture. Its essential question is not: 'Where do we store knowledge?' but: 'How does information become governed knowledge and subsequently legitimate action, while preserving uncertainty, authority, and lineage?'
rows.statement: Step 201 verdict: the vocabulary exercise's strongest result is that KnowledgeOS is not primarily a data model but a semantic transition architecture, whose essential question concerns how information becomes governed knowledge and legitimate action while preserving uncertainty, authority, and lineage.

rows.anchor: T-007 | ... Canonical Vocabulary Freeze v0.1 (19 definitions with DDD role + invariant) + 22 typed relations ... De-facto current canonical core of the raw track — vocabulary+relations only, no theorems, no proofs

sources.note: The Step 287 research programme (explicitly research/falsification, not canonical) for identifying candidate invariants of the KnowledgeOS state-transition system, following Step 286's ontology: a generic invariant schema, a 12-item candidate matrix (I-01..I-12), a four-category taxonomy (Identity/Typing/Transition/Layer), a mandatory vacuity/falsification protocol, a four-way independence classification, and an explicit list of ten things Step 287 must not do.

rows.anchor: $$ \boxed{ \text{Candidate invariant} \not\Rightarrow \text{Canonical invariant} } $$ Each proposed invariant must survive: 1. source interpretation, 2. KnowledgeOS translation, 3. formal typing, 4. equality specification, 5. independent derivation, 6. falsification, 7. classification.
rows.statement: Establishes Step 287 as explicitly a research/falsification step, not a canonical-invariant step: a candidate invariant does not imply a canonical invariant, and each proposed invariant must survive seven stages (source interpretation, KnowledgeOS translation, formal typing, equality specification, independent derivation, falsification, classification) before promotion.

rows.anchor: $$ \boxed{ \mathcal I(P): \forall K,o. Admissible(o,K) \Rightarrow (P(K)\Rightarrow P(\delta(K,o))) } $$ ... These questions must be answered before calling \(P\) an invariant.
rows.statement: Gives the generic invariant schema I(P): for all K,o, Admissible(o,K) implies (P(K) implies P(delta(K,o))), and states this schema itself requires answering: what is the state domain, what is the equality relation, what transitions are included, is P structural/semantic/provenance-sensitive/observational, and is P universal or scoped to a particular transition class.

rows.anchor: | I-01 | Knower identity persists | Identity | **Strong candidate** | | I-02 | Relevant provenance survives derivation | Transition / lineage | **Open** | | I-03 | Admissibility is outcome-independent | Governance / predicate | **Supported** | | I-04 | Command ≠ Transformation | Typing | **Supported** | | I-05 | Validity ≠ Outcome | Predicate separation | **Supported** | | I-06 | Knower ∉ observed state | Layer/ontology | **Supported candidate** | | I-07 | Reality ≠ Observation | Layer | **Supported** | | I-08 | Observation ≠ Interpretation | Layer | **Supported candidate** | | I-09 | Unknown/conflicting/unresolved are preserved at observation layer | Observation | **Candidate** | | I-10 | Semantic state preservation under selected transformations | Semantic | **Open** | | I-11 | Provenance-sensitive preservation | Provenance | **Open** | | I-12 | Universal state invariant independent of observer | Observation | **Open / likely too strong** |
rows.statement: Proposes a 12-item candidate invariant matrix (I-01 through I-12) spanning Identity, Typing, Transition/lineage, Governance/predicate, Predicate separation, Layer/ontology, Observation, Semantic and Provenance categories, each with a current status (Strong candidate / Open / Supported / Supported candidate / Candidate / likely too strong); explicitly states the final invariant set must not yet be inferred from this table.

rows.anchor: Identity invariants ... Typing invariants ... Transition invariants ... A fourth category may be required: Layer invariants
rows.statement: Proposes a four-category invariant taxonomy under I: Identity invariants (N persistence, provenance), Typing invariants (Command≠δ, N∉K), Transition invariants (P(Kt)->P(Kt+1), admissibility, lineage), and Layer invariants (Reality≠Observation, Observation≠Knower, Observation≠Interpretation); explicitly frames whether these all legitimately belong to one mathematical object I as itself a Step-287 research question.

rows.anchor: **No invariant may be stated without a transition scope.** ... $$ \boxed{ \forall (K,o)\in T_P: P(K) \Rightarrow P(\delta(K,o)) } $$
rows.statement: Extends the equality-typing discipline to scope: no invariant may be stated without an explicit transition scope T_P (which transitions preservation is claimed over — every transformation, every admissible one, every authorized one, etc.), refining the invariant schema to quantify only over (K,o) in T_P.

rows.anchor: $$ \boxed{ Invariant(P) \text{ is relation-relative where }P\text{ compares objects} } $$ For example, a transformation can preserve semantic state ... while changing ... structural
rows.statement: Argues that any invariant comparing objects is relation-relative among the four equality relations (=, ≡, ≈, ≅_λ): a transformation can preserve semantic state (K_t ≡ K_{t+1}) while changing structurally (K_t ≠_structural K_{t+1}) because metadata/representation changed, and provenance-sensitive equality may distinguish states that semantic equality identifies.

rows.anchor: Step 287 must distinguish: $$ \text{invariant} $$ from: $$ \text{conserved information} $$ ... This distinction prevents the persistence research from accidentally collapsing into state immutability.
rows.statement: Distinguishes an invariant (P(Kt) implies P(Kt+1)) from a conservation claim (a stronger statement about preserved content or quantity): the existence of Lineage does not imply every aspect of the previous state is conserved, and N persisting does not mean K_t=K_{t+1} — preventing identity-persistence research from collapsing into state immutability.

rows.anchor: For every invariant: 1. establish that the antecedent can actually hold; 2. establish that the transition class is non-empty; 3. establish that the equality relation permits meaningful comparison; 4. only then evaluate preservation. Thus: **No vacuous invariant counts as substantively established.**
rows.statement: Generalizes the D285-5 vacuity lesson into a mandatory four-step vacuity check for every candidate invariant: establish the antecedent can actually hold, establish the transition class is non-empty, establish the equality relation permits meaningful comparison, and only then evaluate preservation — no vacuous invariant counts as substantively established.

rows.anchor: ### Independent ... ### Corroborated ... ### Philosophical analogy ... ### Unsupported ... This preserves: $$ \boxed{ \text{corroboration}\neq\text{derivation} } $$
rows.statement: Defines a four-way independence classification for each candidate invariant: Independent (KOS derivation alone), Corroborated (KOS derivation plus Gita correspondence), Philosophical analogy (Gita distinction without independent KOS necessity), Unsupported (no valid derivation) — preserving the rule that corroboration is not the same as derivation.

rows.anchor: Step 287 must not: * introduce new invariants because they appear philosophically attractive; * turn every architectural constraint into a mathematical invariant; * treat provenance as automatically immutable; * assume semantic equality includes \(\Pi\); * assume observational equality without defining the observation set; * use theological propositions as falsification results; * repair rejected \(\Theta\) constructions; * introduce \(\mathcal K_{\text{ātma}}\); * introduce a universal Knower into the formal KnowledgeOS model; * declare the invariant set complete merely because candidate tests have passed.
rows.statement: Lists ten explicit prohibitions for Step 287: no introducing invariants merely because they are philosophically attractive; no converting every architectural constraint into a mathematical invariant; no treating provenance as automatically immutable; no assuming semantic equality includes Pi; no assuming observational equality without defining the observation set; no using theological propositions as falsification results; no repairing rejected Theta constructions; no introducing K_atma; no introducing a universal Knower into the formal model; no declaring the invariant set complete merely because candidate tests passed.

rows.anchor: ### G-I1 — What is the exact carrier of \(\mathcal I\)? ... ### G-I2 — What counts as a transition? ... ### G-I3 — Which equality applies? ... ### G-I4 — Which invariants are independent? ... ### G-I5 — Which invariants are temporal versus ontological?
rows.statement: States five open research gaps that Step 287 begins with: G-I1 (what is the exact carrier/domain of I — predicates over K_t only, or over (K_t,o,Pi,N,O)?), G-I2 (what counts as a transition delta — commands, events, human actions, system transformations, governance decisions?), G-I3 (which of the four equality relations applies to each preservation claim?), G-I4 (which invariants are independently required versus merely restating architecture?), G-I5 (which invariants are temporal preservation laws versus ontological/typing laws, e.g. N∉K is not obviously temporal while Command≠δ is fundamentally a typing law)?

rows.anchor: Step 286 answered: **What exists?** Step 287 asks: **What must remain true?**
rows.statement: States the final boundary distinguishing consecutive steps: Step 286 (Ontology) answered 'what exists', Step 287 (Invariant Research) asks 'what must remain true', and only a future step ('Invariant Canonization') may promote I from a research construct to a canonical KnowledgeOS component, once candidates are typed, tested, falsified where possible, and classified.

rows.anchor: **We can write STEP 287 now, but we must not pretend that every proposed invariant is already a KnowledgeOS invariant.**
rows.statement: Given D288's finding that several foundations (≡, ≈, ≅_λ decision procedures; Qualify; O enumeration; 8-primitive minimality) remain formally unresolved, argues Step 287 can establish which invariants are derivable from the current corpus and ontology, but cannot legitimately conclude these are the final invariants I of KnowledgeOS — doing so would prematurely promote research into architecture, exactly what D288 forbids.

rows.anchor: distinguish state invariants from qualification invariants ... $$ Observation \rightarrow Qualification \rightarrow Evidence $$ cannot simply be collapsed into: $$ Observation \Rightarrow Knowledge $$ because `Qualify` remains unresolved.
rows.statement: Argues Step 287 should distinguish state invariants from qualification invariants: the chain Observation -> Qualification -> Evidence cannot be collapsed into Observation implies Knowledge, because Qualify remains unresolved; likewise the mere existence of an ontology does not automatically make every ontological relation an invariant.

rows.anchor: if we encounter something of the form $$ K_1 \equiv K_2 \Rightarrow P(K_1)=P(K_2) $$ we cannot call that a final invariant until the semantics of `≡` are fixed. ... any invariant relying upon observational equality must carry that parameter. rows.statement: Requires that any candidate invariant using an unresolved equality relation be marked explicitly conditional: a semantic-equality-based invariant is not final until ≡'s semantics are fixed; an observational-equality-based invariant must carry its query/observation-set parameter Q explicitly; a provenance-sensitive invariant must remain conditional until 'relevant provenance' is formally specified.

sources.note: A follow-on bridge experiment (KR-BRIDGE-02, varying the Pi x Q grid per the KR-BRIDGE-01 recommendation) that discovered two declared-vs-effective observable read-set failures: Pi_value_set actually reads the tag field (the same field Q reads) under T_D_relational via a rank computation, and Pi_arity actually reads v under T_C_dedup via deduplication membership, both found only by perturbation testing, not by code inspection. Proposes candidate FR-003 (effective-read closure: read-sets must be computed through actual transformation provenance, never taken from declaration).

rows.anchor: Pi_value_set was declared to read the value field. Under T_D_relational its value is computed from rank, and rank is produced by ordering values within a tag group -- so the observable was in fact carried by tag, the very field Q reads. It did not know this. Neither did I, and I wrote it.
rows.statement: Reports a KR-BRIDGE-02 (Pi x Q grid) finding that the observable Pi_value_set, declared to read only the value field, actually derives its value under transformation T_D_relational from a rank computed by ordering values within a tag group -- so it was in fact carried by the tag field, the very field the inquiry Q reads, an undetected coupling that violates the target/observable-independence discipline established for the bridge experiments.

rows.anchor: the corrected map was still wrong: Pi_arity reads no field by declaration, and after T_C_dedup it reads v -- because arity is a function of which records survive, and membership is decided by a field. A perturbation test found this; reading the code did not.
rows.statement: Reports a second, subtler provenance error even after the first was corrected: Pi_arity, declared to read no field, actually reads the v field after transformation T_C_dedup because arity depends on which records survive deduplication and survival is decided by that field, a coupling found only by a perturbation test (changing one input field and observing which outputs move) and not by reading the implementation code.

rows.anchor: The structural point, stripped of its soteriology: the agent's account of its own activity is not the activity. Pi reports {v}. Pi is in fact carried by {v, tag}. Its self-description is sincere and wrong, and its wrongness is not visible from inside itself -- it is visible only from the transformat
rows.statement: Reads Gita 3.27 as corroborating the shape of the KR-BRIDGE-02 failure: an observable's declared self-description (Pi reports {v}) can be sincere yet wrong (Pi is actually carried by {v,tag}), and this wrongness is not visible from inside the declaration itself, only from the transformation that actually constitutes the observable.

rows.statement: Reads Gita 4.17 ('the way of action is deep/impenetrable') non-mystically as corroborating that dependency structure is not surface-readable: two of three declared provenance maps in this cycle were wrong despite reading the very code that produced them each time.

rows.statement: Registers candidate FR-003 (effective-read closure: an observable's read-set must be computed through the transformation's actual provenance, never taken from its declaration), established by the KR-BRIDGE-02 experiment itself with the lens only naming it after the fact; registers 'declaration != verification' as a standing experimental obligation [PROP] with two independent occurrences now (KR-BRIDGE-01's T_B label mismatch and KR-BRIDGE-02's provenance failures), explicitly noting two occurrences is not promotion per ES-006.1; and rejects both non-doership as a kernel stance (no mechanical content) and 'action's depth' as an argument for interpretive humility in the kernel (legitimate only as a reason to test, which is already an obligation).

rows.anchor: We have experimentally separated three things that we previously tended to mix together: information elimination, preservation of a business inquiry, and successful realization by a decoder. Eliminability != Preservation != Realization.
rows.statement: Confirms the three-way separation of Eliminability, Preservation, and Realization as the strongest result of the KR-REP-REDUCTION/KR-ZERO assessment, restating the formal three questions (can the business question be answered: H(Q|R)=0; can something be eliminated: Zero_{T,Pi}; can the decoder recover the answer: O(R)=Q(D)).

rows.anchor: Every future mathematical statement in KnowledgeOS must carry its epistemic status: Definition, Theorem, Corollary, Empirical Result, Proposition, Conjecture, Refuted, or Open. rows.statement: Proposes making it a permanent methodological rule that every future KnowledgeOS mathematical statement carry an explicit epistemic-status tag (Definition, Theorem, Corollary, Empirical Result, Proposition, Conjecture, Refuted, or Open), to prevent accidentally promoting an experiment into a theorem.

rows.anchor: The original read-disjointness gate was unsound. It checked declared source-field reads, but transformations can derive output fields from other fields. The corrected gate has to operate on the actual transformed representation and be verified empirically.
rows.statement: Reports that KR-BRIDGE-02 discovered its own original read-disjointness gate was unsound because it checked declared source-field reads while transformations can derive output fields from other fields (matching the Pi_value_set/tag coupling found in the companion Gita study), requiring the corrected gate to operate on the actual transformed representation and be verified empirically rather than by declaration.

rows.statement: Judges KR-BRIDGE-02 a significant methodological strengthening of the research program precisely because it caught its own measurement/gating assumptions wrong twice (the read-disjointness gate and the marginal-RD adjudication criterion) rather than merely producing another numerical result.

rows.anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
rows.statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

rows.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
rows.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

rows.anchor: No Zero/preservation bridge exists for read-disjoint (Π, Q).
rows.statement: Standing conjecture with an explicit refutation condition (one substantive, replicating, gate-clean cell with |MH-RD|>=0.01 on both splits); stated so it can be attacked rather than hardening into an assumption.

rows.anchor: Read-disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T) and verified empirically.
rows.statement: FR-003, CANDIDATE this cycle, established by KR-BRIDGE-02 §2 catching a false positive (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) that a hand-inspected provenance map (wrong twice) would otherwise have let through; needs a second independent adopter before promotion per ES-006.1.

rows.anchor: Zero predicts preservation [NEG] — 4 independent tests
rows.statement: Refuted claims about the bridge: Zero does not predict preservation (4 independent tests), Zero does not mark the reduction boundary, admissibility is a property of (Pi,Q,T) not (Pi,Q), read-disjointness cannot be established by declaration, and neither flattening the redundancy distribution nor raising population size increases informative strata.

rows.anchor: The one substantial effect in the entire grid was an artifact of shared reads.
rows.statement: KR-BRIDGE-02's instrument failed twice before reporting anything: first a marginal-RD adjudication falsely reported 'H2 SUPPORTED, 27/27 replicate' (re-finding the known confounder), then a naive read-disjointness gate let through an inadmissible cell (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) caused by rank=f(value,tag) leaking into Pi; a second, corrected gate was itself found unsound by perturbation testing (Pi_arity effectively reading value via dedup survivorship), yielding the rule 'admissibility is a property of the TRIPLE (Pi,Q,T), never of the pair' and 'declaration is not verification.'

rows.anchor: Causal inference can estimate: What happens? It cannot, by itself, determine: What ought we value? ... Therefore KnowledgeOS needs a clean separation: FACTUAL/EMPIRICAL -> Causal knowledge -> CONSEQUENCES -> NORMATIVE/GOVERNANCE -> Decision.
rows.statement: Wisdom Lens #7 Values: causal analysis can estimate consequences (e.g. Policy A: +10% efficiency/-20% autonomy vs Policy B: +5% efficiency/+20% autonomy) but cannot decide which value should dominate without a normative framework; KnowledgeOS needs a clean Factual/Empirical -> Causal knowledge -> Consequences -> Normative/Governance -> Decision separation, called 'enormously important for AI governance.'

rows.anchor: An AI agent might say: 'The evidence indicates X improves productivity, therefore you should implement X.' Wisdom architecture should reject that leap. ... The AI may assist every stage. But it should not silently collapse them.
rows.statement: Protects KnowledgeOS from AI overreach: an AI agent asserting evidence directly implies a decision ('X improves productivity, therefore you should implement X') must be rejected; the correct chain is Evidence -> Causal assessment -> Consequences -> Applicable values/constraints -> Decision authority -> Decision, with AI able to assist every stage but never silently collapse them.

rows.anchor: AI: discover evidence, formulate questions, construct causal hypotheses, identify assumptions, run analyses, expose uncertainty, generate options, simulate consequences -> HUMAN/GOVERNED JUDGMENT -> DECISION. ... The platform supplies the epistemic scaffolding. Governance supplies legitimate authority. The agent supplies reasoning assistance.
rows.statement: AI architecture principle: an AI agent should not be the source of wisdom; it discovers evidence, formulates questions, constructs causal hypotheses, identifies assumptions, runs analyses, exposes uncertainty, generates options and simulates consequences, but human/governed judgment produces the decision -- the platform supplies epistemic scaffolding, governance supplies legitimate authority, the agent supplies reasoning assistance.

rows.statement: AST-018's core business principle: the human speaks business language and never operates workflow mechanics (UUIDs, REGISTER, HANDOFF, START, predecessor, mutation owner, transition JSON); Governance/Communication capabilities perform the mechanical consequences of business decisions through the canonical workflow mechanism.

rows.anchor: Responsibility ≠ Authority; Eligibility ≠ Authorization; Recommendation ≠ Appointment; Appointment ≠ Activation; Activation ≠ Work completion; Workflow state ≠ Business decision; Evidence ≠ Authority; Identity ≠ Authority
rows.statement: Eight critical non-equivalences the capability must preserve, most centrally: the system may recommend a next actor, but only an explicit human decision constitutes an appointment, and appointment itself is not yet activation.

rows.anchor: inferring 'Yes' because the user asked for a reviewer prompt; treating an AI message as humanAct without an explicit human act; auto-appointing because one candidate exists; auto-starting a session merely because it was selected
rows.statement: Four named invalid inferences of human authority are explicitly forbidden: inferring consent from an unrelated request, treating an AI message as the human act, auto-appointing a sole candidate, and auto-starting a selected session; the human decision remains the sole authority act, and the orchestrator only automates mechanics after it exists.

rows.statement: The process recording a commission for a fresh implementation session is explicitly barred from spawning a subagent to fill that role, because a subagent inherits the parent session's identity and therefore cannot satisfy the freshness/independence requirement for appointment.

rows.anchor: Empirical probe 2026-08-22: a subagent spawned from this session reports CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID = b51dba91-6fc4-4110-b2f2-ac76ad0f3808 (parent's identity inherited; distinct OS PID only)
rows.statement: An empirical probe finds that a subagent spawned from a Claude Code session reports the parent session's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID rather than a distinct one (only the OS PID differs), establishing that a subagent can never serve as a 'fresh, independent' actor for appointment purposes; the fresh actor exists only when the PO/ARB starts a genuinely new session.
